Competition Commission of India
CCI approves acquisition of certain equity share capital of Great White Global Pvt Ltd by ISAF III Onshore Fund, India Special Assets Fund III, Special Situation India Fund, others and related transactions
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 9:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved acquisition of certain equity share capital of Great White Global Private Limited by ISAF III Onshore Fund, India Special Assets Fund III, Special Situation India Fund, Mr. Mehul Jadavji Shah, Ms. Julie Mehul Shah and Mehul Shah HUF and related transactions.

 

The proposed combination pertains to-

  1. the proposed acquisition of 50% of the issued and paid-up equity share capital of Great White Global Private Limited (Great White) by the ISAF III Onshore Fund, India Special Assets Fund III and Special Situation India Fund (collectively, EAAA Acquiring Entities) and Mr. Mehul Jadavji Shah, Ms. Julie Mehul Shah and Mehul Shah HUF (collectively, Continuing Promoter) (including through the Great White Holdings Private Limited (Acquisition SPV), to be implemented through a series of inter-connected steps, including the subsequent merger of the Acquisition SPV with and into Great White (Great White Transaction); and
  2. the proposed acquisition of sole control over ITVIS Innovations Private Limited (ITVIS) by Mr. Mehul Shah (ITVIS Transaction).

The Great White Transaction and the ITVIS Transaction are collectively referred to as the Proposed Combination.

The EAAA Acquiring Entities are schemes of irrevocable and contributory determinate trusts registered with Securities and Exchange Board of India as an alternative investment fund (AIF) / scheme of an AIF, and are managed by EAAA India Alternatives Limited (EAAA) in its capacity as their investment manager. EAAA is one of India’s leading multi-strategy alternative asset management platforms and is directly controlled by entities which are wholly owned subsidiaries of Edelweiss Financial Services Limited.

 

The Acquisition SPV is a private limited company incorporated in India recently, solely for the purpose of implementing the Proposed Transaction.

The Continuing Promoter comprise of Mr. Mehul Shah and Ms. Julie Shah, who are Indian resident individuals, and the Mehul Shah HUF.

Great White is primarily an Indian fast-moving electrical goods (FMEG) and electrical infrastructure products company. It is also engaged in the manufacture and sale of beauty and personal care (BPC) products such as shaving blades, shaving foam, razors, shaving cream and aftershave lotion.

ITVIS is a private limited company incorporated in India and is engaged in the design, development, supply, and integration of intelligent lighting solutions, lighting automation products, smart electrical and sensor-based systems, and energy-efficient lighting technologies.

Detailed order of the Commission will follow.

2311682.title: Department of Expenditure Launches Special Campaign 6.0 to Institutionalize Swachhata, Clear Pending References
2311682.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Department of Expenditure Launches Special Campaign 6.0 to Institutionalize Swachhata, Clear Pending References
Preparatory Phase Begins for Special Campaign 6.0; Implementation to Run Throughout October 2026
Department Reports Significant Pendency Reduction Since Special Campaign 5.0; Targets Set for Further Action in Campaign 6.0
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 9:14PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Expenditure announced the launch of Special Campaign 6.0, a focused two‑phase drive to institutionalize Swachhata measures and expedite disposal of pending references across the Department and its attached organizations. The Preparatory Phase of the campaign will be conducted from 15th to 30th September 2026, followed by the Implementation Phase from 2nd to 31st October 2026.

All Divisions of the Department along with organizations under its administrative control — Controller General of Accounts (CGA), Chief Adviser (Cost), Central Pension Accounting Office (CPAO), and Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM) — have been sensitized to identify targets during the preparatory phase. Targets include cleanliness (Swachhata), space management, scrap disposal, record management, and early disposal of pending references. The structured preparatory arrangements are intended to ensure systematic, result‑oriented action during the Implementation Phase.

The Department reaffirmed its commitment to administrative efficiency and sustained cleanliness, noting the success of Special Campaign 5.0 (2nd to 31st October 2025). The momentum from the previous campaign continued beyond its formal period and contributed to measurable reductions in pendency. Between December 2025 and August 2026, the Department achieved the following disposal outcomes:

• MP references disposed: 57

• Comments furnished on Inter‑Ministerial References (Cabinet Note): 339

• State Government references addressed: 1,123

• Public grievances redressed: 2,788

• Public grievances appeals resolved: 141

The Department of Expenditure expressed confidence that Special Campaign 6.0 will further strengthen internal processes, enhance transparency, and improve service delivery. Officers and staff have been urged to actively participate in both phases and to adopt best practices for sustainable cleanliness and record management.

2311643.title: Union Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav celebrates Sewa Diwas with School Children, lights ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ under ‘Sewa Sankalp Abhiyan’
2311643.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2311643.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav celebrates Sewa Diwas with School Children, lights ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ under ‘Sewa Sankalp Abhiyan’
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 8:12PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav today interacted with school children in New Delhi on the occasion of Sewa Diwas, under the ‘Sewa Sankalp Abhiyan – Aashirwad Ka Diya’ programme. The event was graced by MLA (Mehrauli), Shri Gajender Yadav; Secretary, MoEFCC, Shri Tanmay Kumar; Director General (Forest) and Special Secretary, MoEFCC, Shri Sushil Kumar Awasthi besides senior officers of the Ministry.

The event was organized by the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) to commemorate 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s selfless service to the people of the country. It sought to promote the spirit of Sewa Bhav (selfless service) among communities, particularly the younger generation, while fostering awareness about forests, wildlife, nature and environmental conservation. The programme brought together school students, teachers, eco-club members, government officials and local communities.  As part of the programme, school children presented an environment-themed song.

A large Rangoli incorporating Diyas was prepared to symbolise light of knowledge, hope, service and environmental responsibility being carried forward by the younger generation. The Minister also reviewed an exhibition of selected paintings by school children, depicting themes related to environment, forests, wildlife and nature.

2311630.title: Semicon 2.0 to deepen India’s semiconductor ecosystem with focus on design, equipment, fabs, advanced packaging, R&D and talent
2311630.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Semicon 2.0 to deepen India’s semiconductor ecosystem with focus on design, equipment, fabs, advanced packaging, R&D and talent
Around ₹1 lakh crore investment commitments received; close to 1 lakh new employment opportunities expected across the ecosystem
Semicon 2.0 to scale semiconductor design ecosystem, strengthen precision manufacturing and train 1 lakh technicians
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 7:54PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, today outlined the implementation approach and emerging investment momentum under Semicon 2.0, highlighting the Government’s focus on developing the complete semiconductor ecosystem in India.

Addressing the media during SEMICON India 2026, Shri Vaishnaw said that while Semicon 1.0 focused on laying the foundation for India’s semiconductor industry, Semicon 2.0 is aimed at putting the wider ecosystem in place and scaling capabilities across the semiconductor value chain.

The Minister said that investment commitments of around ₹1 lakh crore (approximately USD 11–12 billion) have already been received under the Semicon 2.0 ecosystem. These commitments are expected to translate into significant economic activity and employment, with close to 1 lakh new employment opportunities expected to be created across the semiconductor ecosystem. The investments are expected to materialize over the next two to three years, with companies announcing their respective investments as and when they receive the required board and shareholder approvals.

 

Six pillars to deepen the semiconductor ecosystem

The Minister outlined the Six broad pillars through which Semicon 2.0 will deepen India's semiconductor capabilities:

  1. Design ecosystem:
    The first pillar focuses on scaling India's semiconductor design ecosystem by supporting both start-ups and large companies. The approach will include support for scaling fabless companies, access to funding and venture capital, customer discovery and stronger protection of intellectual property.

The Government is targeting 200 semiconductor design start-ups under the expanded approach. The Minister noted that 20 of the 105 semiconductor start-ups supported during the first phase have already secured Venture Capital funding, describing this as a significant achievement and a basis for scaling up the target under Semicon 2.0.

The design ecosystem will also support companies in moving beyond individual chip design towards systems design, enabling Indian talent and companies to address increasingly complex technology requirements.

  1. Machines and materials:
    The second pillar will strengthen India's ecosystem for semiconductor manufacturing equipment, machines and materials.

The Minister highlighted the growing interest of global capital equipment companies in establishing operations in India, including capabilities for design as well as manufacturing. He said that India's established design capabilities can support global equipment manufacturers in setting up design operations, generating high-quality employment for Indian youth.

Companies establishing manufacturing operations can also benefit from India's developing precision manufacturing ecosystem, which serves multiple sectors including aerospace, aviation, semiconductors and advanced electronics.

  1. Fabs:
    The third pillar focuses on expanding semiconductor fabrication capabilities across different technologies, including display, memory, silicon, compound and logic fabs. The Minister said that confidence among global semiconductor companies is increasing and that interest in establishing semiconductor manufacturing capabilities in India is growing.

 

  1. Advanced packaging:
    The fourth pillar focuses on advanced semiconductor packaging capabilities. With increasing importance of advanced packaging in improving efficiency and system-level performance, the Government will support the development of capabilities in this area as an important part of India's semiconductor ecosystem.
  2. Research and Development:
    The fifth pillar will promote applied R&D involving industry, government and academia. Under this approach, industry will be encouraged to propose R&D projects, with funding participation from industry and Government and involvement of academic institutions. The objective is to develop applied technologies and achieve tangible outcomes that can strengthen India's semiconductor capabilities.
  3. Talent development:
    The sixth pillar focuses on expanding India's semiconductor talent base. The Minister said that around 400 universities and institutes are already engaged in semiconductor chip-design education under the first phase. Semicon 2.0 will seek to upgrade the curriculum so that students who acquire foundational chip-design capabilities can also progress towards systems design.

In addition, the Government has set a target of training 1 lakh technicians over five years. This will involve partnerships with industry and international institutions, including institutions such as ITRI, Taiwan, to establish training capabilities aligned with the requirements of India's emerging semiconductor manufacturing facilities.

 

 

Focus on building the ecosystem around semiconductor manufacturing

The Minister emphasised that the objective of Semicon 2.0 is not limited to establishing individual semiconductor manufacturing facilities but to build a complete ecosystem around them.

He highlighted the importance of developing domestic capabilities in capital equipment, materials, gases, chemicals, precision manufacturing and supply chains. Such capabilities, he said, would help create a deeper and more resilient semiconductor ecosystem and support India's long-term growth in the sector.

The Minister also highlighted the growing importance of resilient global supply chains and said that India is seeing increasing interest from semiconductor companies looking to diversify and strengthen their supply chains.

Global competitiveness remains central to semiconductor manufacturing

The Union Minister said that global competitiveness in terms of quality and cost has remained a key consideration from the selection of semiconductor projects through construction and production.

He said that the semiconductor facilities that have entered commercial production are competing in the global market, with production capacity being taken up by customers. He also noted the rapid pace of capacity creation at the facilities currently being established.

 

11 MoUs and 5 Announcements to strengthen semiconductor value chain

As part of SEMICON India 2026, 11 MoU exchanges and announcements were undertaken covering semiconductor manufacturing, packaging, materials, equipment, design, talent development and related ecosystem capabilities.

Key agreements and announcements included:

  1. Suchi Semicon Pvt Ltd and eInfochips Pvt Ltd exchanged the first batch of commercial devices.
  2. Tata Electronics and Nexperia B.V. entered an MoU covering semiconductor wafer manufacturing, assembly and test, technology collaboration and innovation.
  3. Tata Electronics and Ascendas First Space entered an MoU for developing a 363-acre vendor park to accelerate the semiconductor fab supplier ecosystem in Dholera, Gujarat.
  4. Tata Electronics and Fujifilm Corporation entered an MoU to support localisation of critical semiconductor materials for India's semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem.
  5. Tata Electronics and JSR Corporation entered an MoU for supply of photoresists and advanced chemicals for Tata Electronics’ fab in Dholera, Gujarat.
  6. Tata Electronics and BESI Singapore Pte. Ltd. entered an MoU focused on building advanced semiconductor packaging capabilities in India.
  7. Tata Electronics and Semiconductor Laboratory (SCL) entered an MoU covering semiconductor design services, process technology, supply-chain localisation and talent development.
  8. Tata Electronics and Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, in collaboration with L&T EduTech and Jacobs Solutions, entered an MoU for talent development in semiconductor facility engineering and infrastructure systems.
  9. Kaynes Semicon and OptoML India entered an MoU to jointly develop advanced semiconductor packaging and System-on-Module solutions.
  10. Kaynes Semicon, GridCrest Technologies and Sensesemi entered an MoU to explore opportunities in packaging, assembly and testing.
  11. India Semiconductor Mission and Intel India launched an ‘Introduction to Semiconductors’ course.
  12. Intel India and New Age Makers' Institute of Technology (NAMTECH) entered into an MoU for developing a future-ready workforce in AI and semiconductor technologies.
  13. HORIBA inaugurated its HORIBA KOACH Experience Centre.
  14. Sensesemi Technologies Private Limited, Bengaluru and GridCrest Technologies Private Limited, Delhi entered into an MoU for smart metering solutions.
  15. Six ChipIN Regional Centres were announced for expanding access to chip-design capabilities and democratising semiconductor design across the country.
  16. Announcement of commercial production of CDIL semiconductors and association for development of packages with Shindengen Electric Manufacturing Company, Japan.

 

India’s semiconductor journey moves towards a full-stack ecosystem

According to the Minister, the semiconductor industry is highly complex and requires sustained efforts across multiple layers of the value chain. Semicon 2.0 has therefore been designed to build capabilities not only in chip manufacturing but also in design, equipment, materials, advanced packaging, research, talent and supply chains.

He said that India's semiconductor journey will require a calibrated and long-term approach, with the objective of establishing an ecosystem capable of supporting sustained growth over the coming decades.

The Government's approach under Semicon 2.0 is aimed at enabling India to emerge as a trusted and resilient participant across the global semiconductor value chain while creating high-quality employment and strengthening domestic technological capabilities.

SEMICON India 2026 which runs till September 19th at Yashobhoomi , New Delhi, features more than 600 participating companies and is expected to attract around 50,000 visitors, with representatives from 52 countries, more than 400 executives and over 150 speakers. The exhibition features six Country Pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, along with 12 State booths, a Startup Pavilion, Innovation Showcase, Student Hackathon and Workforce Development Pavilion.

*****

2311623.title: 43rd Indian Coast Guard Commanders’ Conference: Raksha Rajya Mantri calls upon ICG to remain prepared for emerging maritime challenges by keeping pace with rapid technological advancements
2311623.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
43rd Indian Coast Guard Commanders’ Conference: Raksha Rajya Mantri calls upon ICG to remain prepared for emerging maritime challenges by keeping pace with rapid technological advancements
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi

The 43rd edition of Indian Coast Guard (ICG) Commanders’ Conference commenced in New Delhi from September 17, 2026. On the opening day of the three-day conference, Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth interacted with DG ICG Director General Paramesh Sivamani and Coast Guard Commanders on pivotal issues concerning national and maritime security. In his address, Raksha Rajya Mantri commended ICG for safeguarding maritime interests by ensuring coastal security and being the first responder in times of distress at sea, saving precious lives irrespective of the nationality. He called upon ICG to remain prepared for emerging maritime security challenges by keeping pace with rapid technological advancements.

Highlighting that the character of warfare and security challenges are changing rapidly, Shri Sanjay Seth stressed the growing importance of networks, sensors, software, data, Artificial Intelligence, autonomous systems, cyber capabilities and space-based technologies. Stressing the need to harness emerging technologies to enhance operational effectiveness, he called for ICG to not only remain a user but also become a co-creator by working closely with start-ups, industry, DRDO and research institutions.

“Aatmanirbharta is not merely about buying Indian; it is about developing solutions for Indian challenges and creating capabilities that can meet global requirements. This embodies our vision of ‘Make in India, Make of World’,” added Raksha Rajya Mantri.

Raksha Rajya Mantri highlighted the ICG’s crucial role in Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) operations that contribute to the safety and well-being of people at sea. He stated that the capabilities developed for maritime security also play an important role in search and rescue, medical evacuation, disaster response and pollution control.

Shri Sanjay Seth underscored the importance of strengthening India’s maritime capabilities across the spectrum, from the littoral and green waters to the open oceans and blue waters, in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions). He stressed the need for advanced platforms, underwater technologies, unmanned systems, long-endurance surveillance capabilities, satellite-enabled maritime domain awareness and secure communications. “As India’s maritime responsibilities expand, our capabilities must expand with them, from our coasts to the wider maritime domain,” he said.

During the conference, the ICG Commanders will also interact with Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani and Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, fostering inter-service collaboration across the full spectrum of maritime security. The discussions will further promote the growth, capability development, and infrastructure expansion of ICG.

The deliberations at the conference provide a distinguished platform for ICG Commanders to comprehensively review operational preparedness, material and logistical support, HR development, training, and administrative initiatives undertaken over the past year. It helps them to identify vital milestones essential for safeguarding maritime interests, against the backdrop of evolving geopolitical dynamics and complexities of maritime security. Over the course of the conference, the Commanders will assess ongoing projects aimed at strengthening indigenisation through ‘Make in India’ initiative, in alignment with the Government’s vision of ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’.

2311596.title: Union MoS Raksha Khadse reviews sports development in West Bengal; assures SAI support to strengthen grassroots sports and athlete pathways
2311596.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2311596.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Union MoS Raksha Khadse reviews sports development in West Bengal; assures SAI support to strengthen grassroots sports and athlete pathways
Inspects SAI Regional Centre Kolkata; interacts with athletes and coaches, reviews Sports Science facilities and new Khelo India hostel; discusses strengthening sports development
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports Smt. Raksha Khadse visited the Sports Authority of India (SAI) Regional Centre at Salt Lake, Kolkata, and reviewed the sports infrastructure, athlete development facilities and support systems available at the Centre.

During the visit, Smt. Raksha Khadse paid floral tribute at the Netaji Subhash Bust and subsequently visited the hockey field, where she interacted with trainees and coaches and took feedback on their training, facilities and competitive requirements. She also visited the indoor facilities for gymnastics and table tennis and interacted with athletes and coaches.

Smt. Khadse visited the Sports Science Department and interacted with sports science staff, reviewing the role of scientific support in athlete development, conditioning, recovery and performance enhancement. The interaction was attended by senior SAI officials, including Regional Director, SAI Kolkata, Shri Sibananda Mishra, Olympians Smt. Soma Biswas and Smt. Poulami Ghatak, Regional Director, MY Bharat, Shri Dev Kumar Chatterjee, and members of the Indian Women’s Rugby Team. She emphasised the importance of integrating sports science, nutrition, rehabilitation and performance support with quality coaching and regular competition exposure.

The Minister also inspected the new 300-bedded Khelo India hostel and reviewed the accommodation and support infrastructure being developed for athletes. She subsequently visited the archery field and athletics facilities, interacting with coaches and trainees and taking stock of their training requirements.

Following the facility inspection, Smt. Raksha Khadse chaired a review meeting with SAI officials on the functioning of the Regional Centre, including athlete development, infrastructure, coaching, sports science and support systems. She assured continued support from SAI in strengthening sporting opportunities at the grassroots and developing stronger pathways for young athletes to progress towards higher levels of competition.

Smt. Khadse emphasised that West Bengal’s rich sporting culture and talent base can be further strengthened through quality infrastructure, scientific training, quality coaching and greater competition exposure. She highlighted the importance of ensuring that young athletes have access to the facilities, training and support systems required to pursue sporting excellence.

ABOUT SAI KOLKATA

The SAI Eastern Regional Centre serves as an important regional hub for implementing and monitoring SAI schemes across West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Tripura and Andaman & Nicobar Islands. The Centre has extensive sporting infrastructure including hockey and football fields, an archery field, a 400-metre synthetic athletics track, swimming pool, basketball and volleyball courts, as well as indoor facilities for gymnastics and table tennis. 2311593.title: Third BIMSTEC Conference on Traditional Medicine Concludes in Goa
2311593.body_html:
AYUSH
Third BIMSTEC Conference on Traditional Medicine Concludes in Goa
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 7:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Third BIMSTEC Conference on Traditional Medicine Knowledge, Genetic Resources and Intellectual Property Rights and the Second BIMSTEC Nodal Group Meeting concluded today in Goa, with participation from all seven BIMSTEC Member States.

 

Day 2 continued with a visit to AIIA Goa, showcasing its state-of-the-art facilities in tertiary care and academics, with delegates sharing institutional best practices. A plantation programme was also organised, symbolising the shared commitment to traditional medicine and biodiversity conservation.

 

The Nodal Group deliberated on and arrived at four key areas of cooperation covering institutional and policy cooperation; standards and trade; documentation and capacity building; and implementation mechanisms. All Member States unanimously agreed to support each other in the areas of intellectual property, genetic resources and traditional medicine knowledge, providing a strong foundation for continued regional cooperation.

 

Prof. Vaidya P.K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, said that the conference was significant as it moved beyond discussions to consensus on several important issues, with the ‘Goa Conclusions’ providing a strong foundation for future BIMSTEC cooperation.

 

Smt. Monalisa Dash, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, appreciated the active participation and constructive cooperation of all Member States.

 

Mr. Kadirkamu Kandasamy Yoganaadan, Director, Science, Technology & Innovation and Health and Human Resource Development Division, BIMSTEC Secretariat, appreciated the Ministry of Ayush and AIIA Goa for the successful organisation, coordination and hospitality, noting that regional cooperation ultimately seeks to improve people’s well-being and preserve traditional medicine heritage for future generations.

 

The Vote of Thanks was delivered by Prof. Dr. Sujata Kadam, Dean, AIIA Goa, who expressed gratitude to all BIMSTEC Member States, delegates, experts, officials and stakeholders for their active participation and contribution to the successful conclusion of the conference.

2311580.title: Ministry of Power launches “Special Campaign-6” to institutionalize Swachhata and minimize pendency
2311580.body_html:
Ministry of Power
Ministry of Power launches “Special Campaign-6” to institutionalize Swachhata and minimize pendency
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi

In line with the Government’s initiative to institutionalize Swachhata and minimize pendency in government offices, the Ministry of Power (MoP), along with its Subordinate Offices, Attached Offices, Autonomous Bodies and CPSUs, have been actively participating in the Special Campaigns since the year 2021.

This year’s campaign will place special emphasis on "Effective Collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste" in strict adherence to the guidelines of the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022. Alongside e-waste disposal, the drive will ensure timely clearance of pending matters relating to MP's References, References from State Governments, Inter-Ministerial communications, Parliamentary Assurances, PMO references, Public Grievances, and PG Appeals (CPGRAMS).

The Preparatory Phase of the “Special Campaign-6” has commenced w.e.f. 15th September, 2026 and will continue till 30th September, 2026. During the Preparatory Phase, the MoP and its Subordinate Offices, Attached Offices, Autonomous Bodies and CPSUs, will identify the pendency in selected parameters, mobilize the ground functionaries, finalize cleanliness campaign sites, review records, undertake space management planning and identify scrap material for disposal. Nodal Officers in the CPSUs and other Organisations of MoP have already been nominated.

The Implementation Phase of the ‘Special Campaign 6’ will be from 2nd October to 31st October, 2026, during which efforts will be directed towards achieving targets set in the Preparatory Phase for Swachhata and reducing pendency.

On 16th September 2026, Secretary (Power) chaired a meeting to review the preparations for “Special Campaign 6.0”, which was attended by senior officers of the Ministry of Power and its CPSEs/organisations.

While commending the sustained efforts of the Ministry and its CPSEs/organisations under the Campaign since 2021, Secretary (Power) urged all concerned to maintain the momentum and set new benchmarks in institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency. He expressed the hope that the Campaign would continue to promote cleanliness, boost morale, enhance work place and improve work culture.

2311571.title: CBDT and its subordinate offices to undertake Special Campaign 6.0 for Swachhata and efficiency
2311571.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
CBDT and its subordinate offices to undertake Special Campaign 6.0 for Swachhata and efficiency
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India is launching Special Campaign 6.0 for Swachhata in Government offices and disposal of pending matters from 2nd to 31st October 2026.

The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, along with its subordinate offices across the country, will actively participate in this transformative initiative led by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG).

The foundation for Special Campaign 6.0 rests on the achievements of its predecessor, Special Campaign 5.0, during which the CBDT carried out the cleanliness campaigns at 1,521 sites, disposing of 2.30 lakh physical files, more than 10,000 e-files. During Special Campaign 5.0, the Income Tax Department freed 1.67 lakh square feet of office space and generated ₹32 lakh through scrap disposal. Most importantly, over 21,251 public grievances were resolved, reaffirming CBDT's commitment to transparency, responsive governance, and citizen-centric service delivery.

To carry forward the spirit of the Special Campaign 5.0, CBDT resolved to further continue the positive steps taken for the resolution of public grievances during the campaign. As part of the same, the CBDT resolved 52,290 public grievances and disposed of more than 6,776 grievance appeals during the period from December 2025 to August 2026. This demonstrates CBDT's commitment to responsive governance.

Under Special Campaign 6.0, CBDT will concentrate on four key areas that align with India's digital transformation and sustainable development goals:

  • Disposal of e-waste
  • Record management
  • Space optimisation & office beautification, and
  • Accelerated grievance redressal

 

The CBDT remains steadfast in its commitment to Swachhata, transparency, and efficient service delivery. These initiatives align seamlessly with Government guidelines to institutionalise Swachhata and enhance citizen services.

2311557.title: SECL Honours 75 Workers on Vishwakarma Jayanti and Birthday of Prime Minister
2311557.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
SECL Honours 75 Workers on Vishwakarma Jayanti and Birthday of Prime Minister
Sanitation workers felicitated under Swachhata Hi Seva; SECL sets targets for Special Campaign 6.0
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 6:28PM by PIB Delhi

South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL), a subsidiary of Coal India Limited, organised the second SECL Vishwakarma Awards at its Headquarters in Bilaspur today on the occasion of Vishwakarma Jayanti and the birthday of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. A total of 75 regular and contractual workers were felicitated for their exemplary contribution to mining, operations, maintenance, supervision and other technical activities.

During the program sanitation workers were also felicitated under the ongoing Swachhata Hi Seva Special Campaign 6.0.

The programme was attended by Shri Biranchi Das, Director (Human Resources), SECL; Shri Ramesh Chandra Mohapatra, Director (Technical/Operations); and Shri Nripendra Nath, Director (Technical/Projects & Planning), Additional Charge, along with representatives of trade unions and various employee associations, HoDs, Officers and employees from SECL’s operating areas.

At the start of the program , a message from Union Minister for Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy for coal workers was also read out. The message acknowledged the contribution of coal workers towards the country’s energy security and development and appreciated their hard work and dedication.

Sanitation Workers Felicitated under Swachhata Hi Seva – Special Campaign 6.0

As part of Swachhata Hi Seva and Special Campaign 6.0, sanitation workers engaged in maintaining cleanliness and hygiene across SECL establishments were also felicitated during the programme. The initiative recognised their contribution to maintaining clean and well-organised workplaces and highlighted the importance of dignity of work and collective responsibility towards cleanliness.

Under Special Campaign 6.0, SECL has set measurable targets for cleanliness, waste management, space optimisation and record management. The company has identified 225 sites for cleanliness activities, covering approximately 40 lakh square feet, and has set a target for disposal of 3,300 metric tonnes of scrap.

With effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste as the key focus of Special Campaign 6.0, SECL will undertake systematic e-waste management activities across its establishments. The campaign will also target review of 500 physical files, weeding out of 200 physical files, review of 7,000 e-files and closure of 3,000 e-files.

2311551.title: Secretary, MSDE inaugurates Skills4Future (Shell India) EV & Green Skills Lab at NSTI Bengaluru
2311551.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
2311551.body_html:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Secretary, MSDE inaugurates Skills4Future (Shell India) EV & Green Skills Lab at NSTI Bengaluru
EV & Green Skills Lab under Shell’s Skills4Future programme marks a step towards strengthening the vocational training ecosystem through industry-aligned training in electric vehicle technologies and sustainable mobility
The initiative is a collaborative effort of Shell India, Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the aegis of MSDE for equipping students and faculty with future-ready capabilities in green energy and e-mobility
Skills4Future programme has impacted over 290 institutes, trained more than 70,000 learners, and established 20 Green Skills EV lab across five states
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening India's green skilling ecosystem, Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, IAS, Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) inaugurated the Skills4Future EV & Green Skills Lab at the National Skill Training Institute (NSTI), Bengaluru recently. The lab has been established under the Skills4Future programme, a collaborative initiative of Shell India, Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) and Edunet Foundation, aimed at equipping youth with future-ready skills in Electric Vehicles (EVs) and green technologies.

During her visit, Secretary, MSDE, interacted with students, trainers and industry representatives, and witnessed quality infrastructure and practical learning modules on EV technology. The facility has been designed to provide learners with hands-on exposure to Electric Vehicle systems, battery technologies, diagnostics, safety practices and other emerging green technologies, thereby enhancing their employability in rapidly growing sectors of sustainable mobility and clean energy.

Speaking on the occasion, Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, IAS, Secretary, MSDE, emphasized the importance of industry-government collaboration in creating a workforce equipped for the jobs of the future. She noted that initiatives such as the Skills4Future programme play a crucial role in preparing young people for emerging opportunities in green mobility, renewable energy and sustainable technologies while supporting India's vision for inclusive and sustainable economic growth.

The Skills4Future programme has emerged as a significant intervention in advancing green and EV skilling across the country. Through partnerships among government, industry and implementation agencies, the programme has already reached more than 290 institutes across five states, trained over 70,000 learners, upskilled over 258 faculty members and established 20 Green Skills EV lab, thereby creating a multiplier effect throughout the vocational education and skilling ecosystem.

In Karnataka alone, the programme has impacted 101 Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), trained 9,113 students, demonstrating its contribution towards creating industry-ready talent for the state's growing green economy. The newly inaugurated EV & Green Skills Lab at NSTI Bengaluru further strengthens this ecosystem by providing advanced training infrastructure and experiential learning opportunities for trainees.

The Skills4Future initiative is aligned with the Government of India's vision of fostering a skilled workforce capable of supporting the country's transition towards green mobility and sustainable development. By integrating industry-relevant curriculum, practical learning infrastructure and placement-linked opportunities, the programme seeks to bridge skill gaps and enable youth to participate meaningfully in emerging sectors of the economy.

The inauguration of the EV & Green Skills Lab at NSTI Bengaluru marks another milestone in the ongoing partnership between MSDE, DGT and Shell India, reaffirming their shared commitment to empowering youth with future-focused skills and supporting India's journey towards a greener and more sustainable future.

2311463.title: India’s Textile exports rise 16.1% to ₹29,776 crore in August 2026
2311463.body_html:
Ministry of Textiles
India’s Textile exports rise 16.1% to ₹29,776 crore in August 2026
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi

India’s textile sector recorded strong export growth in August 2026, with total exports increasing by 16.1% year-on-year to ₹29,776 crore, compared with ₹25,656 crore in August 2025. During April–August 2026, cumulative textile exports reached ₹1.43 lakh crore, registering growth of 10.3% over the corresponding period of the previous year.

The growth was broad-based across several major textile segments. In August 2026, exports of cotton yarn, fabrics, made-ups and handloom products grew by 24.1%, while man-made yarn, fabrics and made-ups increased by 19.9%. Carpet exports recorded growth of 15.0%, while handicrafts, excluding handmade carpets, registered particularly strong growth of 41.4%. Ready-made garments of all textiles also maintained positive momentum, growing by 6.1% during the month.

The cumulative performance during April–August 2026 also remained encouraging, with cotton textiles growing by 18.0%, man-made textiles by 13.6%, carpets by 11.9% and handicrafts by 44.0%.

The sustained growth across major segments reflects the increasing competitiveness and diversification of India’s textile export basket, supported by improved market access, policy interventions and continued efforts towards value addition and market diversification. The sector remains an important contributor to manufacturing, employment and India’s overall export growth.

2311456.title: DFS Launches Nationwide Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign
2311456.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DFS Launches Nationwide Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign
DFS and All Its Organisations Undertake Swachhata Pledge Under the Theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”
SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivirs to Provide Welfare Services, Health Check-ups, PPE Kits and Financial Inclusion Support
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance, launched the nationwide Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign today. Marking the formal commencement of the campaign, Shri Sanjay Lohiya, Secretary (DFS), led the Swachhata Pledge ceremony.

Reaffirming their collective commitment to cleanliness and public health, all organisations under the Department of Financial Services also undertook the Swachhata Pledge on 17.09.2026. The participating entities include Public Sector Banks (PSBs), Public Sector Insurance Companies (PSICs), Public Sector Financial Institutions (PSFIs), Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), State Level Bankers' Committees (SLBCs/UTLBCs), attached and subordinate offices, regulatory bodies including RBI, IRDAI and PFRDA, and Debts Recovery Tribunals (DRTs/DRATs), spanning their nationwide network of offices and branches.

The Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign is being observed across the country from 17th September to 2nd October 2026, guided by the central theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”.

During the campaign, the Department will primarily focus on the following activities:

• Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) & Clean Public Spaces: An operational target has been set to identify, map and remediate over 5,000 Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs)—sites that are difficult to clean and demand concentrated sanitation intervention. Lead District Managers (LDMs) across the nation have been entrusted to coordinate with local administrations, volunteers and civic groups to transform at least 10 critical dirty spots, alongside intensive cleanup of public places, including bus stands, beaches and community toilet complexes.

• SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivirs: Single-window welfare and preventive health check-up camps are being organised for all regular, contractual and outsourced sanitation workers (SafaiMitras) and their dependents. Organisations of DFS will be enrolling SafaiMitras into flagship financial inclusion and social security programmes, prominently the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) and Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), along with the distribution of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits and formal public felicitations.

• Mass Cleanliness Drive — “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, EkSaath”: A nationwide cleanliness drive has been scheduled for 1st October 2026 at 8:00 AM, mobilising employees, bank functionaries, customers and civil society for one hour of collective public sanitation work.

• Jan Bhagidari & Sustainable Waste Management: In accordance with the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2026, all administrative and commercial premises of organisations are enforcing mandatory 4-way source segregation of waste (Dry, Wet, Hazardous, and E-waste). Institutions are establishing collection points for Reduce, Reuse & Recycle (RRR) centres and institutionalising Kabaad Se Jugaad (Waste to Wealth) and Kabaad Se Kala (Waste to Art) exhibits at major administrative buildings and training centres.

• Plantation Drive ('Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam'): Branch networks and offices across the nation are actively carrying out tree plantation activities, planting saplings within and around their premises during the campaign duration.

All planned interventions, baseline data, and geotagged 'before-and-after' visual records are being systematically monitored and will be uploaded by designated Nodal Officers on the dedicated national portal swachhatahiseva.gov.in to ensure end-to-end accountability, transparency and public visibility.

Meetings with the field functionaries, appointment of Nodal Officers, and training for uploading the activities on the portal have been completed. Various meetings and visits are lined up during the campaign period to make it a grand success.

2311453.title: Ministry of Coal Successfully Launches 16th Round of Commercial Coal Mine Auctions; Executes CMDPAs for Six Coal Mines
2311453.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
Ministry of Coal Successfully Launches 16th Round of Commercial Coal Mine Auctions; Executes CMDPAs for Six Coal Mines
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 5:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Coal successfully launched the 16th Round of Commercial Coal Mine Auctions on September 17, 2026, in New Delhi. Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Minister of State for Coal and Mines, graced the occasion as the Chief Guest.

On the occasion, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey launched the 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions and, along with Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, Secretary, Ministry of Coal, handed over Coal Mine Development and Production Agreements (CMDPAs) to the successful bidders of six coal mines auctioned in earlier rounds.

The CMDPAs were executed for Tara (Revised), Margo West, Margo East, Mandla South, Dongeri Tal-II and Dip Side of PKoC. The successful bidders include CG Syn-Gas & Chemicals Ltd., Jharkhand Exploration & Mining Corporation Limited, Qube Commercial Pvt. Ltd., Gallant Ispat Ltd. and The Singareni Collieries Limited.

The six mines together have geological reserves of approximately 1,504 million tonnes and a combined Peak Rated Capacity of 11.62 MTPA. Once operational, they are expected to generate annual revenue of around ₹1,984 crore, attract capital investment of nearly ₹1,743 crore and create approximately 15,700 employment opportunities in the respective coal-bearing regions.

The 16th round offers 25 coal blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines, across nine coal-bearing states—Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Telangana and West Bengal. Of these, six coal mines are offered under the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act (CMSP) and 19 under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act (MMDR). The blocks are open to experienced mining companies, new entrants and technology-driven enterprises under the liberal commercial coal mining framework, which provides for no end-use restrictions, 100% FDI through the automatic route and low upfront payments adjustable against future revenue share.

With the launch of this round, the commercial coal mining programme has now completed sixteen rounds since Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi opened the sector to commercial mining in 2020. A total of 147 coal mines have been auctioned to date, with cumulative expected annual revenue of over ₹47,500 crore and projected capital investment of more than ₹55,000 crore across nine coal-bearing states.

Addressing the launch of the 16th Tranche of Commercial Coal Mine Auctions in New Delhi, MoS for Coal & Mines, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, highlighted coal’s vital role in powering India’s growth, meeting around 55% of the country’s primary energy requirement and over 70% of its electricity generation. Under the guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he underlined the remarkable growth in coal production, which has crossed the 1 billion tonne mark for the second consecutive year, reflecting the strength of India’s domestic coal sector and its growing contribution to energy security.

Shri Dubey highlighted the Government’s efforts to transform the coal sector through greater transparency, competition and technology-enabled processes. He emphasised the importance of providing a level playing field for stakeholders and creating a conducive environment for investment and wider participation in commercial coal mining. He underscored the need to unlock India’s domestic coal resources, enhance production and reduce dependence on imports, while ensuring efficient and sustainable utilisation of the country’s coal reserves. He also called upon stakeholders to actively participate in the commercial coal mine auction process and contribute to strengthening India’s energy security.

 

In her welcome address, Ms. Rupinder Brar, Additional Secretary and Nominated Authority setting the tone of the day she emphasised that transformation of India’s coal sector towards a transparent, technology-enabled and competitive ecosystem. She noted the surge in Coal production in recent years from captive and commercial mines, emphasising that energy is the foundation of growth, development and progress.

Ms. Brar underlined the immense potential of India’s coal sector to unlock domestic resources, drive production, attract investment and create new opportunities. She also emphasised that the Office of the Nominated Authority remains open and accessible to all stakeholders, facilitating dialogue and addressing their concerns and queries to ensure a conducive and transparent framework for commercial coal mining.

 

In his insightful address at the of launch of 16th round of Commercial Coal Mine auctions, Shri  Sanoj Kumar Jha, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Coal, highlighted the growing focus on coal gasification as an important avenue for value addition and innovative utilisation of India’s abundant coal resources. He emphasised the need to accelerate technology adoption and strengthen the ecosystem for next-generation coal utilisation. He also stressed the importance of learning from global best technologies and best practices, while developing solutions suited to India’s requirements. Leveraging technology, innovation and global expertise can help unlock new possibilities in coal utilisation and support a more efficient, sustainable and future-ready coal sector.

The Ministry of Coal remains committed to deepening reforms in the coal sector, promoting greater participation and investment, and ensuring a reliable and affordable energy supply in line with India’s long-term energy security goals

2311451.title: Science Policy and Communication in an Era of Global Challenges: From Boundaries to Breakthroughs
2311451.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Science Policy and Communication in an Era of Global Challenges: From Boundaries to Breakthroughs
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 5:11PM by PIB Delhi

Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) has been organizing annual sessions (virtual mode) during the Science Summit at United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) that are aimed at showcasing CSIR's contributions to Science and Technology and efforts towards Global Sustainable Development. The central theme of SSUNGA81 is "From Boundaries to Breakthroughs: Science for a Regenerative and Equitable Future". With this background, CSIR-NIScPR organised an online session on “Science Policy and Communication in an Era of Global Challenges: From Boundaries to Breakthroughs” on 16 September 2026, bringing together experts and practitioners to deliberate on strengthening the interface between science, policy and society in addressing complex global challenges.

Dr. Naresh Kumar, Chief Scientist, CSIR-NIScPR, in his welcome address emphasized the importance of moving scientific knowledge from research to real-world application and urged the need for stronger institutional mechanisms for connecting research, policy and deployment.

Outlining the overview of the scientific session, Dr. Kasturi Mandal, Senior Principal Scientist, CSIR-NIScPR and convener of the session mentioned the persistent global “science divide” in infrastructure, skills and participation and that the central premise of the session is that science policy and science communication are complementary pillars of sustainable & inclusive development.

Dr. (Mrs.) Geetha Vani Rayasam, Director, CSIR-National Institute of Science Communication and Policy Research (CSIR-NIScPR) chaired the scientific session. She also highlighted the significance of technology readiness, scientific entrepreneurship and foresight on emerging technologies, particularly in view of rapid developments in Artificial Intelligence. She stressed the need to anticipate emerging scenarios and strengthen evidence-informed policy approaches to ensure that scientific and technological advances translate into meaningful societal outcomes.

Shri Rohit Gupta, CTO of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, presented TRL Compass, India's evidence-based national framework for assessing technology readiness, showing how a structured, sector-specific approach can de-risk deep tech investment and offer a template that emerging economies can adapt to their own priorities. He highlighted the collaboration between the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA) and CSIR-NIScPR in development of sectoral specific TRL assessment frameworks for India which could be relevant to global south.

Dr. Joana Ball, Managing Director, Directory of Open Access Journals surged the involvement of governments, funders, researchers, universities, libraries, and publishers in strengthening open knowledge systems. She also highlighted the role of CSIR-NIScPR in connecting Indian research with researchers and wider society.

Dr. Avinash Kshitij, Scientist, CSIR-NIScPR highlighted aligning technological development with societal needs, investment, skills, and market readiness, highlighting technology foresight to anticipate emerging trends and policy priorities. Research shows startups and entrepreneurship can address societal issues through emerging technologies.

Dr. Vinayak, Scientist, CSIR-NIScPR highlighted a complexity-based approach that goes beyond citation counts to identify breakthrough research by exploiting the local structure of citation networks, map which countries are making breakthroughs in which disciplines, and reveal the scientific capabilities of nations.

Dr. Paramananda Barman, Scientist, CSIR-NIScPR discussed the relevance of inclusive science communication, highlighting the barriers such as language, literacy, culture and digital access, approaches and contributions of CSIR-NIScPR for strengthening SciComm.

Dr. Amit Kumar, Assistant Professor, RIS India's narrated India’s successful experience and expertise with technology-led development transformation since it's independence and accentuated to next level through DPI in the recent times has lot of potential to share with the Global South!

 

The session concluded with a shared emphasis on strengthening the connection between scientific knowledge, policy processes and societal needs. The discussions highlighted the importance of collaborative, interdisciplinary and participatory approaches to advancing inclusive, resilient and sustainable pathways for the future.

2311428.title: Ministry of Finance to organise a Conference of State Finance Ministers and Finance Secretaries on “Financing India’s Journey towards Viksit Bharat” on 18th and 19th Sept. 2026 in New Delhi
2311428.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Ministry of Finance to organise a Conference of State Finance Ministers and Finance Secretaries on “Financing India’s Journey towards Viksit Bharat” on 18th and 19th Sept. 2026 in New Delhi
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 4:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Finance will organise a Conference of Finance Ministers and Finance Secretaries of States and Union Territories with Legislature on “Financing India’s Journey towards Viksit Bharat” on 18th and 19th Sept. 2026, in New Delhi. The Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs will be present during the conference. Several Chief Ministers and Finance Ministers from the States will participate along with senior State officials in the conference.

The Conference on Financing India’s Journey Towards Viksit Bharat will be on the policy complementarities between the Centre and the States, and will bring together academic rigour and practical policy to deliberate on financing challenges and policy priorities for India’s development journey.

Smt. Anuradha Thakur, Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), Ministry of Finance, will briefly highlight the objectives of the conference at the inaugural session.

The keynote address at the inaugural session will be delivered by Shri N.K. Singh, President and Life Trustee, Institute of Economic Growth, and Chairman, 15th Finance Commission (XVFC). Shri Sudhir Shrivastava, former Additional Chief Secretary and Finance Secretary, Government of Maharashtra, will present the State’s perspective on financing Viksit Bharat.

The conference will have three thematic sessions:

 

  • Macroeconomic overview
  • Financing agricultural transformation
  • Financing the energy transition

 

Providing the context for these two-hour deliberations are background papers that have been circulated to the participants on topics such as macroeconomic milestones and pathways towards Viksit Bharat, Private financing for Viksit Bharat, Implications of GST 2.0 for States; Financing agricultural markets and marketing, Financing resilience and sustainable resource use in Indian agriculture; Financing renewable energy and transmission assets, and Financing carbon capture utilisation and storage, among others.

Additionally, Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), will highlight importance of measuring growth outcomes in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat; and Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), will briefly highlight the role of new-age technology in good governance.

2311398.title: Vice President Pays Tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and the Heroes of the Hyderabad Liberation Struggle at the Hyderabad Liberation Day Celebrations
2311398.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Vice President Pays Tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and the Heroes of the Hyderabad Liberation Struggle at the Hyderabad Liberation Day Celebrations
Hyderabad Liberation marks a significant chapter in the nation’s journey: Vice President
Firm resolve of Sardar Patel, courage of armed forces and struggle of people of Hyderabad strengthened national unity: Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 4:22PM by PIB Delhi

At a grand ceremony held today at Secunderabad Parade Ground on the occasion of Hyderabad Liberation Day, Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan recalled the historic chapter of the integration of the erstwhile princely state of Hyderabad into India and paid tribute to all the heroes who fought for the unity and integrity of the nation.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that the story of Hyderabad is, in many ways, the story of the making of India. He added that the integration of the erstwhile princely state of Hyderabad into a unified India on September 17, 1948, marked a significant chapter in the nation’s journey of nation-building. He noted that it was part of the journey of national unity and nation-building that strengthened the foundations of modern India. He also recalled and paid homage to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel for his decisive role in the integration of the princely states.

 

Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, while paying tribute to the martyrs, said that it was the firm resolve of Iron Man Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the indomitable courage of the armed forces, and the unwavering desire of the people of Hyderabad to merge with India, coupled with their struggle, that brought the region into the fold of national unity. He also highlighted the contribution of the brave soldiers of the Jodhpur Lancers in this struggle.

Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar said that the people of Hyderabad had suffered under the Nizam’s rule and the atrocities committed by the Razakars. He said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, with firm resolve, freed them from this tyranny and made Hyderabad an integral part of India.

At the ceremony, 10 contingents of the Central Armed Police Forces presented a march past. The historical and cultural context of Hyderabad was presented through a special cultural performance on the theme “Hyderabad Vimochanam”. On the occasion, the winners of the Hyderabad Liberation Day Quiz Competition, held at the Salar Jung Museum, were felicitated by the  Vice President.

The Vice President visited a special exhibition organised by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting at the venue, showcasing historical episodes connected with Hyderabad Liberation Day and the journey of national unity.

On the occasion, Telangana Governor Shri Shiv Pratap Shukla, Union Minister of Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Malkajgiri MP Shri Etala Rajender, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Shri Vivek Aggarwal, and Director General, Central Reserve Police Force, Shri Gyanendra Pratap Singh, among other dignitaries, were present.

The Hyderabad Liberation Day celebrations, while commemorating a significant chapter of history, also underscored the role of citizens in nation-building, the constitutional values of equality, dignity and opportunity, and the resolve to continuously strengthen India’s unity.

***

2311395.title: Shivraj Singh Chouhan Plants Saplings with Sarpanches on PM Modi’s Birthday, Also Addresses VB–G RAM G Workshop Held at Delhi
2311395.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Shivraj Singh Chouhan Plants Saplings with Sarpanches on PM Modi’s Birthday, Also Addresses VB–G RAM G Workshop Held at Delhi
Fraud in Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Scheme Will Not Be Tolerated at Any Cost – Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
If a Pond Is Already Full and Workers Are Still Being Engaged There, It Is a Matter of Concern; Conduct Random Inspections of Works – Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Technology Has Been Used to Leave No Scope for Fraud; Face Authentication-Based Attendance of Workers Made Mandatory – Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Fake Muster Rolls Used to Be Generated Under MGNREGA; A Worker Would Sit in Delhi While Money Would Be Withdrawn from the Village – Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
While Addressing the Shortcomings of MGNREGA, Provision Made to Provide 100 to 125 Days of Employment to Workers, but the Work Should Contribute to Developing the Village – Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Focus on Building Developed Villages While Following the 60% Wage and 40% Material Norm – Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Let ViksitGaon Be Built for a Viksit Bharat; the Objective of the Scheme Is Not Merely to Dig Soil and Dump It Elsewhere – Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Irregularities of MGNREGA Will Not Be Allowed to Be Repeated Under Viksit Bharat–G RAM G at Any Cost – Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 4:18PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today planted saplings with sarpanches and departmental officials at the Pusa campus in New Delhi on the occasion of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s birthday and extended his birthday greetings to the Prime Minister. Thereafter, the Union Minister addressed the National Workshop organised on Viksit Bharat–G RAM G. The workshop was attended by elected representatives of Panchayati Raj Institutions, Commissioners and senior officials of States and Union Territories, and other participants.

­­­­

On the occasion, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan directed officials to conduct random inspections of works being undertaken under the scheme. Where works are being carried out in accordance with the prescribed standards and procedures, the concerned persons should be appreciated. However, wherever any irregularity is found, strict action should be taken at the very outset so that no one dares to violate the rules in future.

There Will Be No Leniency in Case of Fraud

Union Minister for Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan issued a strong message to the States and Union Territories regarding any kind of fraud and irregularity under the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Scheme. He said that fraud in the scheme would not be tolerated at any cost.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said, “Remember, we will not allow any fraud in this scheme at any cost. I am clearly saying as the Minister that if there is any fraud, no one will be spared. Action will be taken against anyone who indulges in irregularities.” He said that if a pond in a village is already full and workers are still being engaged there, it is a matter that needs to be investigated. He directed officials to keep a close watch on such cases.

Conduct Random Inspections of Works; Take Action at the Very Outset if Irregularities Are Found

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan told officials of States and Union Territories that only two months have passed since the scheme was launched and the third month is underway. Therefore, it is essential to keep the monitoring and inspection mechanism strong right from the beginning. He directed that random inspections of selected works be conducted. Where works are being carried out properly, the concerned persons should be appreciated, while any irregularity found should invite immediate action so that irregularities are curbed at the initial stage and such situations do not recur in future.

Technology Will Help Curb Fraud

The Union Minister said that technology has been used in the scheme to ensure better monitoring of works and to leave no scope for fraud. He said that attendance of workers has now been made mandatory through Face Authentication. Therefore, it should also be ensured through the technological system that there are no gaps in this mechanism.

He said that when a complaint comes to light, it is natural to be concerned. He urged all concerned officials to ensure that no breach occurs at any level in the implementation of the scheme. He said, “All the officials are sitting here, and I want to tell them and the Commissioners to ensure that no one is able to breach the system at any cost.”

Ensure Work for Workers; They Should Not Remain Without Work Even for an Hour

Union Minister for Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the most important objective of the scheme is to provide employment to workers. He said that workers should get work and should not remain without work even for an hour. He also emphasised that timely payment of wages must be ensured. He said that works permitted under the rules should be undertaken after following the prescribed procedures.

He also emphasised adherence to the wage-material ratio under the scheme. He said that at the district level, 60 per cent of the funds are to be spent on wages and 40 per cent on material. Officials were directed to follow the rules and prescribed procedures and prioritise works that create durable and useful assets in villages.

Work Does Not Mean Merely Digging Soil and Dumping It Elsewhere

The Union Minister said that work does not mean merely digging soil at one place and dumping it at another. Keeping in view the objective of “ViksitGaon for a Viksit Bharat”, works under the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Scheme should be considered in a manner that creates a strong foundation for development in villages and strengthens the rural economy.

He told officials that there is now a need to consider how the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Scheme can contribute to building ViksitGaon. Along with providing employment, the scheme should facilitate the creation of assets that remain useful to rural communities over the long term and help make villages self-reliant and developed.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the success of the scheme can be ensured only when workers receive adequate employment, transparency is maintained in the execution of works, fraud is completely curbed, and the scheme also contributes to building developed villages alongside a developed India.

 

National Service Is the Core Mantra of PM Modi’s Life

Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that today is a highly relevant and special day. There is an atmosphere of joy and celebration across the country. Today is the birthday of our Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi. On this occasion, he extended heartfelt greetings and best wishes to the Prime Minister on behalf of rural India.

He said, “My only prayer to God is that Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji may be blessed with a long and healthy life and may he continue to serve the country and its people in the same manner.” He said that national service has remained the core mantra of the Prime Minister’s life.

He said that his journey of public service as the head of government for 25 consecutive years is significant in itself. He served as the Chief Minister of Gujarat and is now leading the nation as the Prime Minister. This long and continuous journey of service is a noteworthy chapter in the history of Indian democracy.

He said that under the leadership of the Prime Minister, the vision of a new India is taking shape—an India that is prosperous, glorious, strong, self-reliant and developed.

***

2311392.title: NHAI Rajmargyatra App Hosts ‘OneTag’ FASTag Portability Service
2311392.body_html:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Rajmargyatra App Hosts ‘OneTag’ FASTag Portability Service
Availability of ‘OneTag’ FASTag portability has expanded the citizen centric services available for National Highway users on Rajmargyatra Mobile App
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 4:15PM by PIB Delhi

In order to enhance consumer choice for FASTag users, ‘OneTag’ - a FASTag portability service is now available on National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) Rajmargyatra App. The initiative enables FASTag users to change their issuer while retaining the existing FASTag affixed to their vehicle, eliminating the need to obtain a new physical tag. The availability of ‘OneTag’ FASTag portability has expanded citizen centric services available for National Highway users on Rajmargyatra App, which include FASTag Annual Pass, FASTag Local Pass, Emergency Helpline 1033 among other services.   

The Rajmargyatra app guides users through the FASTag portability process. FASTag users can login to App and enter their vehicle registration number to check eligibility. The user will receive a verification six-digit Mobile Verification Code (MVC) from current issuer bank. Following authorization, the user will be required to select a new issuer, complete customer verification and wallet onboarding with the new issuer to complete the portability process. Following successful portability, the existing FASTag ID linked to vehicle registration number will remain unchanged, allowing users to continue using the same physical tag with a different issuer bank.

After portability is completed, previous issuer will close the existing FASTag wallet and refund the available balance, post applicable adjustments. Also, interoperable FASTag has a cooling period of 6 months before it can be ported again.

The ‘OneTag’ initiative will help to improve FASTag lifecycle management by reducing the need for repeated tag production, thereby lowering operational costs, dispatching and reissuance expenses. ‘OneTag’ will also help to streamline the issuer-switching journey, enhance customer choice and contribute to a more interoperable and efficient FASTag ecosystem.

With a penetration rate of over 98 percent and around 13 crore users, FASTag has revolutionized the Electronic Toll Collection system in the country. The introduction of ‘OneTag’ will further strengthen the digital tolling architecture and provide FASTag users with greater flexibility, while retaining the existing physical tag and proving greater convenience to the National Highway users.

2311371.title: From Financial Barriers to Academic Progress: Samir Makhal's Journey with NFSC
2311371.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Barriers to Academic Progress: Samir Makhal's Journey with NFSC
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 4:03PM by PIB Delhi

Timely fellowship support enables scholars from disadvantaged backgrounds to continue advanced studies, undertake quality research and work towards better professional opportunities. Financial constraints and limited access often interrupts academic journeys to undertake research work.

Shri Samir Makhal, a 33-year-old scholar from Howrah district in West Bengal, is pursuing a Ph.D. with support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme. The fellowship has helped him meet research and educational expenses and continue his doctoral studies with greater financial stability.

Before receiving assistance, Shri Makhal faced financial difficulties that delayed his research and made it challenging to manage educational and daily expenses. Limited research opportunities, geographical constraints, family responsibilities and inadequate institutional support further affected his progress.

Despite these barriers, he remained committed to higher education and quality research. He aspired to build a successful academic and professional career and improve his socio-economic condition, even as his family faced financial instability and limited access to resources and information relating to higher education.

Shri Makhal began receiving NFSC assistance in May 2020. The fellowship, House Rent Allowance and contingency support helped him meet research expenses, educational costs and daily needs. It also improved his access to study materials, laboratory facilities and other academic resources, enabling him to focus more effectively on his doctoral work.

Following the support, his research work became smoother. Greater financial stability strengthened his confidence and enabled him to pursue his academic and career goals with renewed focus and better professional prospects.

Expressing his satisfaction over the help and support, Shri Makhal said, “NFSC support has enabled me to continue my PhD with greater stability and focus on my academic goals.”

Today, Shri Makhal continues his Ph.D. journey with determination. His experience demonstrates how the NFSC Scheme can help scholars overcome financial and educational barriers and move towards academic excellence and professional growth.

2311348.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Aatmanirbhar Bharat: HAL to hand over LCA Tejas FOC Twin Seater Trainers & HTT 40 Basic Trainer Aircraft to IAF and Dhruv NG helicopters to PHL in the presence of Raksha Mantri & Civil Aviation Minister in Bengaluru

2311342.title: S&T based community initiative improves detection and control of TB in Rajasthan
2311342.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
S&T based community initiative improves detection and control of TB in Rajasthan
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 3:32PM by PIB Delhi

A new, scientific data-based community driven initiative has dramatically improved TB detection and control in remote, underserved regions of Rajasthan. 

Tuberculosis continues to be a major public health problem in many remote areas like the tribal districts of Rajasthan. Factors such as difficult terrain, low awareness, social stigma, seasonal migration, and delayed diagnosis have long hindered TB control efforts and led to TB burden.

In order to address this, AIIMS Jodhpur conducted Cluster based population survey, active case finding, laboratory confirmation to estimate the burden of TB (Active and Latent) among the tribal population and their anti-TB drug resistance pattern.

The study has found ways to limit transmission of TB in the tribal districts of southern Rajasthan, through early detection and streamlining patients to undergo preventive screening through community participation and reaching out with timely treatment. 

Fig: Filed work- screening, sputum collection, Transport and health awareness

 

With support from the SEED division of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), they conducted Household survey, symptom screening, sputum testing, NTEP diagnostics and data analysis among more than 6000 people from Sirohi, Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Dungarpur, Pratapgarh and Banswara districts.

The researchers led by Dr Shoban Babu Varthya (Additional Professor), Department of Pharmacology AIIMS Jodhpur conducted workshops to sensitize people and combined epidemiological survey, grass root level participation of Healthcare workers (HCWs) and panchayat people to improve early detection. Active case finding laboratory confirmation was also undertaken.

People with symptoms of tuberculosis and those with positive results were identified and given treatment for TB as per national guidelines. Besides, community awareness was generated to improve the understanding of TB to help limit the transmission of TB through early detection and streamlining patients to undergo preventive screening among household contacts. This helped enable implementation of TB Mukt Panchayat model with the use of scientific data.

This initiative demonstrates how targeted, scientific research can generate actionable data that directly informs policy and strengthens TB control in vulnerable populations.
