2309950.title: Data Centres in India Infrastructure for the Digital Age
2309950.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Data Centres in India Infrastructure for the Digital Age
Posted On: 14 SEP 2026 11:05AM by PIB Delhi

Data centres are the invisible engines powering India’s digital life. They support banking, e-Governance and online services every second. As emerging technologies drive rapid data growth, the Government is building a supportive policy ecosystem. Infrastructure status, fiscal incentives and clean energy adoption are strengthening India’s data centre ecosystem.

Strengthening India's Digital Infrastructure through Data Centres

India’s digital economy is entering a new phase of rapid growth and technological transformation. Digitalisation is reshaping productivity, competitiveness and service delivery across sectors. As digital services expand, they are generating unprecedented demand for computing capacity, data storage and high-speed connectivity. Meeting this demand requires infrastructure that can operate continuously, securely and at scale. Data centres provide this critical foundation, powering the digital services that increasingly drive India’s economy and governance.

A data centre is a secure facility that houses computing, storage and networking equipment. It stores, processes, manages and distributes large volumes of digital information. These capabilities support online banking, e-Governance, digital payments, cloud computing and other emerging technologies.

Modern data centres integrate computing, networking, power, cooling, security and management systems. These systems work continuously to maintain reliable operations, data security and uninterrupted digital services. As India’s digital economy expands, resilient data centres are becoming a strategic infrastructure for innovation, competitiveness and sustained digital growth.

Inside a Data Centre: The Technologies Powering Digital Services

A data centre relies on a reliable power infrastructure to ensure uninterrupted operation of critical equipment. Data centre computers can never turn off—not even for a millisecond. Uninterruptible Power Supplies (UPS) provide immediate backup during electrical interruptions. Backup generators and electrical distribution systems provide additional resilience during prolonged power disruptions. Continuous operations of this scale requires  cooling systems to maintain suitable operating conditions for the computing equipment. Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems regulate temperature and airflow within the facility. Advanced airflow management and liquid cooling further improve thermal efficiency and reliability.

The Information Technology (IT) infrastructure then performs the core computing functions. Servers process information and run digital applications. Storage systems securely hold large volumes of data using Hard Disk Drives (HDDs) and Solid-State Drives (SSDs). Security systems protect equipment, networks and data from physical and digital threats.

Networking equipment, including routers and high-speed switches, enables data exchange within and beyond the facility. Fiber-optic connections provide high-speed communication between the data centre and external networks.

Finally, management software monitors the systems and helps optimize the use of computing resources efficiently. Virtualisation allows multiple virtual machines to run on one physical server, improving resource use. Imagine taking one large house and dividing it into several separate apartments. Virtualization allows one physical computer to run multiple virtual "mini-computers" inside it, maximizing resource efficiency. Automation tools manage workloads, support maintenance and help identify operational problems.

From Click to Response: How a Data Centre Handles Your Request

Every digital request begins with a simple action, such as opening an app, checking a bank balance or accessing a document. Behind the instant response, the request travels through a network to a data centre, where multiple systems work together to process it securely and efficiently.

The security layer first checks the request and protects the system from cyber threats. The load balancer then directs the request to an available server, helping distribute the workload efficiently.

The application server processes the request and determines what information or service is required. If necessary, it uses an Application Programming Interface (API) to communicate with other applications or services.

The database server then retrieves the required information and sends it back to the application server. Once processed, the information travels back through the network and reaches the user’s device.

This entire process can take just 1–2 seconds, enabling fast and seamless digital services. This interconnected chain— Connect → Receive → Network → Process → Store → Secure → Respond—allows cloud services, e-governance platforms and Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications to deliver information reliably and at scale. It shows why modern data centres are far more than storage facilities; they are the digital infrastructure that enables everyday online services.

In Simple Terms: The Behind-the-Scenes Team

  • Network = The Corridors & Intercom, the internal hallways that connect the whole team so they can pass information to each other instantly.
  • Security Layer = The Security Guard, inspects your request at the entrance for safety.
  • Load Balancer = The Traffic Cop, directs incoming digital traffic so no single server gets overwhelmed
  • Application Server = The Chef, takes your order, figures out what information or recipe is needed.
  • API = The Waiter, acts as a messenger.
  • Database Server = The Digital Vault, where details are locked away and retrieved when needed.

 

Status of Data Centers in India

India’s data-centre journey has evolved alongside the rapid expansion of e-Governance and digital services. Rising citizen expectations for online services are increasing demand for robust data-centre infrastructure. The National Informatics Centre (NIC) has established state-of-the-art National Data Centres across the country. These include facilities at NIC Headquarters in Delhi, Pune, Hyderabad and Bhubaneswar. NIC has also established 37 smaller Data Centres at various State Capitals. These facilities provide reliable digital services to Government institutions at different levels. They support round-the-clock operations, system management and skilled onsite personnel.

India’s rapidly expanding digital economy is further strengthening demand for secure and reliable data infrastructure. Installed data-centre power capacity stood at around 375 MW in 2020. It has increased to 1.57 GW as of August 2026. The capacity is projected to expand further to nearly 8 GW by 2030. Investments of nearly USD 70 billion are already underway in India’s data centre sector, with an additional USD 90 billion in announced projects, highlighting the scale of expansion and reflecting strong investor confidence.

Enabling Policy Environment for Data Centres

The Government has strengthened the data-centre ecosystem through targeted policy and fiscal measures. In the Union Budget 2022–23, data centres were included in the Harmonized List of Infrastructure. This accorded infrastructure status to data centres and facilitated greater access to credit for digital infrastructure. The measure also supported investment and expansion of India’s data-centre capacity.

Infrastructure Status in Simple Terms

Giving data centres "Infrastructure Status" treats them like national highways, airports, and power grids, granting them access to easier and cheaper long-term loans.

The Union Budget 2026–27 further introduced a tax holiday for eligible foreign cloud service providers until 2047. The incentive applies to global operations using India-based data-centre infrastructure. It covers Tax Years 2026–27 to 2046–47 for notified foreign companies. These measures strengthen India’s investment environment for data centres and cloud infrastructure.

Linked Ecosystem Schemes Supporting Data Centre Growth

  • The second phase of the Semicon India Programme (Semicon 2.0) was approved by the Union Cabinet on 15.07.2026, with an outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM). It aims to holistically build a trusted and resilient semiconductor ecosystem in the country.
  • The IndiaAI Mission was approved with a total budget outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore to build a comprehensive AI ecosystem in the country. The AI ecosystem being fostered under the Mission is a key driver of data centre growth in India.
  • The Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) has also received higher financial support. Its allocation increased from ₹22,000 crore to ₹40,000 crore.
  • The Government of India has also launched PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware to create a robust domestic manufacturing ecosystem for IT hardware (such as servers), attract large investments, reduce import reliance, and make India a trusted global supply chain hub.

Sustaining the Data Centre Sector: Energy and Water Planning

Data centre capacity is expanding rapidly, making energy and resource efficiency increasingly important. Data centres require reliable electricity and efficient cooling systems for continuous operations. According to the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Ministry of Power, demand could reach 17 GW by 2031–32. As the sector is expanding, the Government is also promoting cleaner energy and efficient resource use to support sustainable sectoral growth.

Renewable Energy & Clean Power

The Government is promoting renewable energy through several key initiatives. These include the Green Energy Open Access Rules, Green Energy Corridor Scheme and National Green Hydrogen Mission. The National Programme on High Efficiency Solar PV Modules and Solar Park Scheme further support clean-energy deployment. These measures improve access to cleaner and more reliable power for energy-intensive digital infrastructure.

SHANTI Act & Clean Power

The Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act strengthens the clean-power ecosystem. It supports reliable nuclear power for emerging sectors, including Artificial Intelligence and data centres. The framework also enables future deployment of Small Modular Reactors and Micro Nuclear Reactors.

BIS Standards for Data Centres

The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has developed standards for data-centre efficiency. Its technical committee LITD 31 covers Cloud Computing, Information Technology and Data Centres. BIS has published standards covering Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) and Carbon Usage Effectiveness (CUE). These standards also address Cooling Efficiency Ratio (CER) and Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE).

In Simple Terms

PUE and WUE - serve as green mileage ratings to measure how efficiently a facility uses electricity and water.

CUE measures how much carbon pollution a data centre produces for every bit of electricity its computers use.

CER measures how efficiently the cooling systems (like fans, chilled water pipes, or liquid coolant) remove that heat relative to the electricity they consume.

Energy and Water Efficiency Standards

The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) has notified the Energy Conservation Building Code (ECBC) 2017. It also notified the Energy Conservation and Sustainable Building Code (ECSBC) 2024. These codes prescribe energy-efficiency and water-conservation norms for buildings. They also include provisions relevant to data-centre infrastructure.

Advanced Cooling and Water Management

Data-centre water requirements depend on the cooling technologies deployed. Groundwater extraction, including for industrial purposes, is regulated under guidelines issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. AI infrastructure is driving adoption of advanced cooling technologies in data centres. These include direct-to-chip liquid cooling, adiabatic cooling and immersion cooling. Closed-loop liquid cooling systems are also emerging as resource-efficient solutions.

Way Forward

India’s data-centre growth reflects a steady policy journey towards a resilient and sovereign digital infrastructure. It is increasingly important for data sovereignty, digital trust, economic competitiveness and technological self-reliance. The expansion of cloud and Artificial Intelligence infrastructure is creating new opportunities for innovation and economic growth. However, this growth also requires responsible governance of data, technology, energy and digital infrastructure. A technology governance approach can help balance innovation with security, sustainability, accountability and public interest. This requires strong standards, robust cybersecurity, responsible data practices and efficient resource management. It also calls for greater domestic capabilities across computing, semiconductors, energy and critical digital infrastructure. As India advances towards Viksit Bharat by 2047, data centres can serve as a foundational layer of the digital economy.

2309882.title: Shri Bhupender Yadav reviews progress of Great Indian Bustard Conservation, Grassland Restoration and Project Cheetah at Bhuj; Releases Gujarat Action Plan for GIB Conservation
2309882.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2309882.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Shri Bhupender Yadav reviews progress of Great Indian Bustard Conservation, Grassland Restoration and Project Cheetah at Bhuj; Releases Gujarat Action Plan for GIB Conservation
Conservation succeeds when we Restore Whole Landscapes, Not Isolated Species: Union Environment Minister
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 8:51PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today chaired a Review Meeting of Flagship Programmes at Bhuj, Kachchh (Gujarat), covering the conservation status of the Great Indian Bustard, grassland restoration and Project Cheetah. The Review Meeting was also attended by Shri Arjun Modhwadia, Cabinet Minister for Forest and Environment, Climate Change and Science & Technology, Government of Gujarat. Senior officials of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, the Gujarat Forest Department, the Wildlife Institute of India and the National Tiger Conservation Authority were also present.

On the occasion, the Union Minister emphasised that conservation must move beyond individual species to the restoration of entire landscapes, combining scientific management, habitat restoration and community participation, and said India is working towards becoming a global benchmark in landscape-level conservation.

Shri Yadav highlighted renewed efforts to conserve the Critically Endangered Great Indian Bustard (GIB) in Gujarat, where, he noted, Kachchh supports an important but small and isolated population. Releasing the Gujarat Action Plan for GIB Conservation, prepared by the Wildlife Institute of India in collaboration with the Gujarat Forest Department, the Minister said it provides a science-based roadmap to establish a minimum viable population of over 30 birds and secure 200–500 sq. km. of safe, contiguous habitat. He added that the immediate focus is on the approximately 200 sq. km. Lala–Rawa landscape, with interventions including habitat restoration, grazing management, invasive species removal, predator management and mitigation of infrastructure-related threats.

Shri Yadav informed that significant on-ground action has already been undertaken to secure this population. He noted that in Naliya, around 11 sq. km. of grassland infested with the invasive Prosopis juliflora has been restored, and the enclosure secured with 30 km of predator-proof fencing covering 15 sq. km., alongside targeted management of nest predators. Shri Yadav further emphasised that GIB conservation is ultimately the conservation of Kachchh's open natural ecosystems, which, he said, also support the lesser florican, chinkara, desert cats, raptors, vultures and other specialised wildlife.

Referring to a pioneering ‘jump-start’ intervention, in which infertile eggs laid by wild GIB females were replaced with viable eggs from the conservation breeding programme, the Minister said the resulting chick from the second such attempt has survived beyond the critical first three months in the wild – a landmark result for the species' recovery in Gujarat. He further stated that a GIB Soft Release Centre has been developed near Naliya, which will house and acclimatise captive-bred birds from Rajasthan ahead of their eventual release, once appropriate protocols and habitat conditions are in place.

On Grassland Restoration, Shri Yadav underlined the ecological importance of grasslands, which, he said, cover nearly 24% of India's land area but remain among the country's most degraded and under-conserved ecosystems. He informed that a proposed five-year national assessment, in collaboration with the Wildlife Institute of India, ICFRE and the Forest Survey of India, with National CAMPA support, would provide a scientific basis for developing a national framework for grassland management, focusing on mapping, ecological assessment, restoration and improved management of Open Natural Ecosystems, including Gujarat's Banni Grassland.

Reviewing Project Cheetah, the Minister noted that India has established a growing population from 29 founder cheetahs, with the population now reaching 52 individuals, including 49 cubs born in India. He observed that the cub survival rate in Kuno, at around 68%, significantly demonstrates the potential for successful population establishment under appropriate ecological conditions. Shri Yadav further noted that the protected habitat for cheetahs has expanded to 3,428 sq. km. through the integrated management of Kuno National Park and Gandhi Sagar, and that Banni Grasslands in Gujarat and Nauradehi Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh have been identified as future release sites. The Minister said the programme is increasingly moving towards landscape-level management, ensuring adequate habitat, prey base and ecological connectivity for the long-term recovery of the species.

2309866.title: Union Environment Minister presides over Workshop on Mangrove Conservation in Bhuj; Releases Key Mangrove Publications and Reviews MISHTI Progress
2309866.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2309866.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Environment Minister presides over Workshop on Mangrove Conservation in Bhuj; Releases Key Mangrove Publications and Reviews MISHTI Progress
Shri Bhupender Yadav stresses Scientific, Site-Specific and Community-Led Mangrove Restoration; Launches Mangrove GIS (MGIS) Portal for Decision Support
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 8:00PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today addressed the Workshop on Mangrove Conservation, Restoration and Sustainable Management held at Bhuj, Kachchh (Gujarat). Addressing the workshop, the Minister emphasised that mangroves must be conserved as living ecosystems, given their importance for coastal biodiversity, fisheries, shoreline protection, climate resilience and livelihoods.

The workshop was also attended by and addressed by Shri Arjun Modhwadia, Cabinet Minister for Forest and Environment, Climate Change and Science & Technology, Government of Gujarat, and Shri Trikambhai Chhanga, Minister of State for Higher and Technical Education, Government of Gujarat, who reaffirmed the State Government's commitment to mangrove conservation and coastal ecosystem restoration under MISHTI.

Reviewing Gujarat's mangrove conservation efforts under the MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes) programme, the Shri Yadav noted the emphasis on restoration, scientific management, community participation and technology-enabled monitoring. He informed that under MISHTI, Gujarat has made significant progress in mangrove restoration, with 27,652 hectares covered against the 2023–27 target of 29,250 hectares, including 12,450 hectares in the ecologically challenging Kori Creek region. He added that site-specific restoration techniques suited to the conditions of Kachchh have been adopted, alongside measures for biodiversity enhancement, seaweed cultivation and sustainable livelihoods.

On the occasion, the Minister released the Coffee Table Book on Kachchh Mangroves and the Mangroves Atlas of Gujarat, and launched the Mangrove GIS (MGIS) Portal, stating that these would strengthen science-based decision-making and monitoring of mangrove habitats across the state. Shri Yadav also felicitated the Guneri Inland Mangrove Village Biodiversity Management Committee, commending its sustained community-led conservation of the Guneri inland mangroves – a rare ecosystem thriving away from the coast – which, he noted, was declared Gujarat's first Biodiversity Heritage Site in January 2025.

The workshop was attended by senior officials of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and the Gujarat Forest Department, along with scientists, conservationists and representatives of local communities engaged in mangrove restoration and coastal livelihood initiatives in Kachchh.

2309852.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addresses 52nd India Gems and Jewellery Awards ceremony in Mumbai as the Chief Guest
2309852.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addresses 52nd India Gems and Jewellery Awards ceremony in Mumbai as the Chief Guest
India will emerge as the global hub for gems and jewellery in the coming years
The award recipients include exporters, manufacturers, bankers and women entrepreneurs; together, they have set new benchmarks for India’s growth
Era of lab-grown diamonds is now set to emerge, with the market expected to grow to nearly 50 times the size of the current diamond market
We must prepare ourselves in such a way that the entire ecosystem and the complete manufacturing value chain for lab-grown diamonds are in the hands of Indians
India should emerge as a pioneering industry in the new era of lab-grown diamonds, and the Modi Government is ready to provide all possible support to achieve this
Nine out of every ten diamonds cut and polished across the world are processed in Surat, city’s traders have not merely cut and polished diamonds; by generating employment for millions, they have also made a significant contribution to the economy and India’s exports
Mumbai, economic capital of the country, has made a significant contribution to establishing the gems and jewellery trade as a key pillar of India’s exports
The resolve of Prime Minister Modi to make India the world’s foremost nation in every sphere by 15 August 2047 has also been embraced by the 1.4 billion people of the country
Whenever India has faced a crisis, jewellery traders have always stood wholeheartedly with society and the nation
The foundation laid for these awards in 1975 has, over the past 50 years, evolved into a prestigious platform for India’s gems and jewellery industry, I congratulate everyone associated with the industry for its continuity, excellence and contribution to providing employment to millions of people
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the 52nd India Gems and Jewellery Awards ceremony in Mumbai as the Chief Guest. Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Eknath Shinde, Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Shri Harsh Sanghavi, and several other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

Addressing the awards ceremony, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that it is a matter of great happiness for him that the Gems and Jewellery Awards, which have continuously contributed to enhancing India’s economy, prosperity and global brilliance, are being conferred on so many distinguished achievers today. He said that this initiative of the India Diamond Board is a reflection of India’s confidence, skill, prosperity and global aspirations. India will emerge as the global hub for gems and jewellery in the coming years.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that when the foundation of these awards was laid in 1975, hardly anyone could have imagined that this small initiative would, five decades later, evolve into a prestigious platform for the country’s gems and jewellery industry, and that the industry would play such a significant role in the growth of the national economy and the expansion of the MSME sector. Shri Shah said that those honoured today include exporters, manufacturers, bankers and women entrepreneurs. Together, they have set new benchmarks for India’s growth.

Shri Amit Shah said that gems and jewellery have always been an integral part of India’s identity. For over 6,000 years, gems and jewellery from India have been traded across the world. The Roman writer Pliny had written that Rome’s treasury was being depleted by its trade in Indian gems and spices, as the wealth earned by Rome was flowing to India through this trade. Shri Shah said that over the centuries, Indian artisans and craftsmen have continually added new dimensions to this tradition. During the medieval period, jewellery craftsmanship received royal patronage and reached new heights. The princely states of Rajasthan and Kolkata gave rise to the distinctive traditions of Kundan and Meenakari. Even today, Jaipur is renowned across the world as the capital of coloured gemstones. He said that any discussion on India’s gems and jewellery industry would remain incomplete without mentioning Surat. Shri Shah said that it is a fact that Surat has played a tremendous role in transforming the face of an entire industry. Nearly nine out of every ten diamonds cut and polished in the world are processed in Surat. He said that the people of Surat have not merely cut and polished diamonds; they have also demonstrated the highest standards of hard work and perseverance. The diamond merchants of Surat have not only provided employment to millions of people, enabled them to become self-reliant and made a significant contribution to the country’s economy and exports, but have also accomplished something even greater. He said that there was a time when it was believed that Kutch and Saurashtra would turn into a desert within fifty years. However, through their determination and relentless efforts to secure water for Kutch and Saurashtra, the diamond merchants of Surat also played a crucial role in saving the entire Saurashtra region.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Mumbai, the country’s financial capital, has made a significant contribution to establishing the gems and jewellery industry as a key pillar of India’s exports. The Bharat Diamond Bourse (BDB) has today emerged as a symbol of India’s gems and jewellery trade across the world.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah, said that the Government led by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has brought about several transformational changes in the country over the past 12 years. He said that in 2014, India was counted among the ‘Fragile Five’; today, it is among the top five economies of the world. He said that the GDP figures for the first quarter of the current financial year were released recently, and with a growth rate of 7.8 per cent, India has emerged as one of the fastest-growing major economies in the world. He said that this transformation has not been limited to economic activity alone; Prime Minister Modi has worked to bring about change across every sector. He said, “Who could have imagined that a terrorist attack would be answered by entering Pakistan’s territory, and that the country would have a Prime Minister capable of taking such a decisive stand?” Whether it was the surgical strike, the air strike or Operation Sindoor, Modi Ji has pursued a defence policy that makes the enemy think twice and tremble at the very thought of attacking India. He said that whether it is the construction of the Ram Janmabhoomi temple, the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, the rejuvenation of Kedarnath or Mahakal Lok, India has accomplished what, for decades, people did not even have the courage to speak about.

Shri Amit Shah said that the transformational changes brought about by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in the field of infrastructure have given a major boost to the economy. Driven by PLI schemes and facilities aimed at promoting exports, India’s exports are continuing to surpass their own records. He said that Prime Minister Modi has given the 140 crore people of the country the confidence and resolve that by 15 August 2047, India will emerge as number one nation in the world across every sector. The people of India have also embraced this resolve. Shri Shah said that wherever global circumstances have changed and trade and commerce have required support, necessary initiatives have been undertaken. The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026 is the latest example of this. Companies engaged in the trading of rough diamonds in specially notified areas have been granted exemption from income tax for a period of 15 years. This marks a major beginning towards establishing India as the world’s rough diamond trading hub.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi recently inaugurated the Bharat Ratnam Mega Common Facility Centre at SEEPZ, Mumbai, as part of the transformational initiatives in the infrastructure sector. Spread across 1.25 lakh square feet, the centre is equipped with state-of-the-art facilities such as 3D printing, casting and refining. He said that the India Jewellery Park is a landmark project that is expected to attract an investment of around ₹50,000 crore and generate direct and indirect employment for one lakh people. The Maharashtra Government has also extended several incentives, including exemption from stamp duty, concessions on electricity and enhanced subsidy rates. He said that in 2025, the industry had reached ₹2.44 lakh crore, accounting for 6.3 per cent of the country’s merchandise exports. The industry is providing direct and indirect employment to around 75 lakh people.

Shri Amit Shah said that India has today emerged as a major source of jewellery imports for the United States, the Middle East, Hong Kong and Europe, and that this journey must be taken forward. He said that the Free Trade Agreements entered into by the Government of India’s Ministry of Commerce with the European Union, the United Arab Emirates, Australia, Oman and the United Kingdom can serve as a major avenue for expanding our trade. He said that with the support of the Government of India, we must move forward with confidence and determination to explore new markets, new avenues of trade and new opportunities. Today, India processes more than 90 per cent of the world’s cut and polished diamonds, which is the strongest testament to the courage and enterprise of India’s jewellery industry.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that times are changing and so are consumer trends, and this transformation presents a significant opportunity for the gems and jewellery trade. He said that jewellers should be prepared to seize the opportunities arising from these changes. He said that the era of lab-grown diamonds is now set to emerge, with the market expected to grow to nearly 50 times the size of the current diamond market. This represents a tremendous opportunity. He said that when the global jewellery trade underwent modernization, India was under colonial rule. Several countries moved ahead of us, including even smaller nations. But with the advent of the lab-grown diamond era, India has the necessary infrastructure, skills, capital and capable entrepreneurs. He said that we must prepare ourselves in such a way that the entire ecosystem and the complete manufacturing value chain for lab-grown diamonds are in the hands of Indians. Whether it is manufacturing the machines, producing lab-grown diamonds, making jewellery, or developing Indian brands and opening showrooms in cities across the world, the entire value chain should be within our reach. He said that Indian jewellery traders are fully capable of achieving this. Shri Shah said that the Government of India has already taken the initiative, while some enterprising traders in Surat and Mumbai have also taken the lead. The Governments of Gujarat and Maharashtra are bringing in supportive policies, and the Government of India will also introduce appropriate policies. He said that from manufacturing the machines to the showroom where the jewellery ultimately reaches a woman’s hand, India must have ownership of the entire ecosystem, and the industry must move forward with this vision and ambition. He said that merely increasing the pace of work will no longer be sufficient; the scale of operations must also be transformed. Shri Shah said that India should emerge as a pioneering industry in the new era of lab-grown diamonds, and Indian brands should become global brands, ensuring a strong presence for India and Indian jewellery traders in this global business. For this, the Modi Government is ready to provide all possible support.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that whenever Gujarat or India has faced a crisis, the jewellery industry has always stood wholeheartedly with society and the nation. The gems and jewellery industry has never shied away from contributing to the advancement and welfare of society. Whether it was a drought, a flood, a cyclone, water conservation, tree plantation, or ensuring that the children of artisans and employees receive education at the finest institutions, the industry has consistently contributed to the progress of society. For this, I wholeheartedly commend and congratulate the industry. He expressed hope that the leading industrial houses, young entrepreneurs and technologists present here would leave with the resolve that, in the diamond world of the future, the entire value chain should be built in India, and that the marketing chain across the world should also be led by Indian brands.

2309851.title: Secretary, DAHD visits CPDO (Western Region), Mumbai; Calls for Strengthening Poultry Infrastructure, Training and Biosecurity
2309851.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2309851.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Secretary, DAHD visits CPDO (Western Region), Mumbai; Calls for Strengthening Poultry Infrastructure, Training and Biosecurity
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 7:43PM by PIB Delhi

 

Shri Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India, visited the Central Poultry Development Organisation (Western Region), Goregaon, Mumbai, today. Dr. Muthukumarasamy B., Joint Secretary, DAHD, and other senior officials of the Department were also present during the visit.

Shri Gangwar reviewed the functioning of CPDO (Western Region), including breeding, hatching, rearing and training activities, and inspected the hatchery, brooder houses, parent stock, feed plant and training facilities. The implementation of the National Livestock Mission (NLM) and other poultry development schemes was also reviewed. The Secretary emphasised the promotion of low-input technology birds, conservation of indigenous poultry germplasm, strengthening of biosecurity measures and modernisation of poultry infrastructure. Shri Gangwar directed that farmer-oriented training and the supply of quality chicks be further strengthened and appreciated the efforts of the CPDO team.

The Secretary interacted with poultry entrepreneurs trained at CPDO, Mumbai. The entrepreneurs shared their success stories and experiences, highlighting the contribution of CPDO’s training programmes towards entrepreneurship development in the poultry sector. Poultry management books in Hindi and Marathi were launched to promote access to technical knowledge and poultry-related learning in regional languages. Successful trainee students of CPDO, Mumbai, were felicitated for their achievements and inspiring success stories.

As part of the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative, the dignitaries planted saplings, reaffirming their commitment towards environmental sustainability and a greener future. The dignitaries also visited the Poultry Gallery and held detailed discussions with officials of the Central Public Works Department (CPWD) regarding the redevelopment of CPDO, Mumbai. The programme concluded with an interaction with final-year BVSc & AH students of Mumbai Veterinary College on opportunities, challenges and emerging prospects in the veterinary and poultry sectors.

The Secretary also visited the Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (AQCS), Mumbai, which plays a critical role in maintaining the country’s biosecurity by preventing the ingress of animal diseases through the import of live animals and animal products. Shri Gangwar reviewed the functioning of the station and took stock of the ongoing and proposed development activities aimed at strengthening its infrastructure and operational capabilities. The visit provided valuable guidance for the future upgradation of CPDO (Western Region), Mumbai, as a Centre of Excellence in poultry development, training and technology dissemination.

2309809.title: DAHD Reviews Lumpy Skin Disease Situation in NCT Delhi; Emphasises Coordinated Vaccination and Disease-Control Measures
2309809.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2309809.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
DAHD Reviews Lumpy Skin Disease Situation in NCT Delhi; Emphasises Coordinated Vaccination and Disease-Control Measures
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India, today reviewed the Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD) situation in the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi in coordination with the Delhi Animal Husbandry authorities. The review focused on the current disease situation, vaccination coverage, surveillance, treatment and strengthening of preventive and disease-control measures.

On 13th September, 2026 Animal Husbandry Commissioner (AHC), Dr. Naveena B. Maheswarappa, reviewed the disease situation with the Delhi Animal Husbandry authorities and emphasised the need for sustained vaccination, active surveillance and timely implementation of disease-control measures. He also stressed for close coordination with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), gaushalas and other stakeholders, particularly for effective management and vaccination of stray cattle and strengthening of biosecurity measures.

The LSD is sporadic in Delhi and presently under control, with low severity and good recovery among affected animals. No mortality has been reported among affected cattle. As on 13th September 2026, around 584 active cases are being reported, mainly among unvaccinated and vulnerable animals, including those with co-morbidities, weak nutritional status or those under stress.

More than 45,950 animals have been vaccinated against LSD in Delhi during 2026. Vaccination and other disease-control measures are continuing, with emphasis on timely vaccination, surveillance, isolation of affected animals, vector control, disinfection and biosecurity.

During the review, DAHD provided technical guidance to the Delhi authorities on vaccination, treatment and animal management and advised strengthening coordination with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), gaushalas and other stakeholders for effective management and vaccination of stray cattle, isolation of affected animals, vector control, disinfection/sanitization and implementation of biosecurity measures including establishment of physical check-post across neighbouring states for movement control.

Wider awareness activities involving animal owners, local representatives, NGOs, schools and other stakeholders were also emphasised to promote vaccination and good animal-husbandry practices.

The Department continues to maintain close coordination with States/UTs, regularly reviews the situation provide necessary assistance for effective prevention, control and containment of LSD. The disease situation across the country continues to be closely monitored.

2309806.title: Prime Minister meets the Chairperson of the African Union and President of Republic of Burundi on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi
2309806.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister meets the Chairperson of the African Union and President of Republic of Burundi on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi held a bilateral meeting today with H.E. Évariste Ndayishimiye, Chairperson of the African Union and President of the Republic of Burundi, on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.

The two leaders, while recalling India’s role in bringing the African Union into the G20 fold during India's presidency in 2023, stressed that the India-African Union partnership is a key pillar of cooperation within the Global South. They discussed the early convening of the 4th India-Africa Forum Summit (IAFS-IV) at a mutually convenient date.

Prime Minister commended the AU leadership for successfully combating the Ebola Outbreak. The AU Chairperson appreciated the medical support from India to Africa CDC to help in mitigating the outbreak.

The two leaders discussed India-Burundi ties, which continue to be defined by warmth, solidarity and shared developmental aspirations. The two leaders reviewed bilateral ties in the areas of economic cooperation, development partnership, agricultural modernization, healthcare and capacity-building initiatives.

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi met H.E. Mr. Cyril Ramaphosa, President of the Republic of South Africa on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on 13th September 2026.

The two leaders reviewed the progress achieved in diverse areas of cooperation and exchanged views on the multi-faceted strategic partnership between India and South Africa. They affirmed that the close and longstanding relations between India and South Africa is rooted in shared historical struggles, strong cultural affinities, robust economic ties, and deep people-to-people connections. The two leaders exchanged views on a range of global issues of mutual interest and agreed to maintain close coordination in multilateral fora. In the context of the successful translocation of cheetahs from South Africa to India, Prime Minister invited South Africa to consider joining the International Big Cat Alliance.

President Ramaphosa thanked PM Modi for the warm hospitality extended to him and his delegation as well as for the successful organization of the BRICS Summit.

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi met with the Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, H.E. Mr. Kashim Shettima Mustapha, GCON, on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit held in New Delhi. They reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the India-Nigeria Strategic Partnership.

Prime Minister Modi and Vice President Shettima Mustapha also exchanged views on regional and global matters of mutual interest, including priorities and concerns of the Global South. They emphasized the importance of strengthening cooperation in multilateral fora and working together towards a more representative, inclusive and multi-polar international order.

Prime Minister Modi highlighted India's continued commitment to strengthening its partnership with Nigeria and to deepening India's engagement with Africa. Vice President Shettima Mustafa appreciated India's development experience and its contribution to capacity building and economic development in Nigeria.

The meeting reaffirmed the shared commitment of India and Nigeria to building a stronger, forward-looking partnership, contributing to peace, prosperity and development in both countries and in the wider Global South.

2309800.title: LOKAYAN 2026 – INDIAN NAVAL SHIP SUDARSHINI SETS SAIL FROM LIVORNO, ITALY
2309800.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
LOKAYAN 2026 – INDIAN NAVAL SHIP SUDARSHINI SETS SAIL FROM LIVORNO, ITALY
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 6:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Navy’s sail training ship, INS Sudarshini, set sail from Livorno, Italy, on 12 Sep 2026 on completion of a successful port call. During her stay, the ship participated in a series of professional interactions and cross-training visits, strengthening bonds of friendship and maritime partnership between the two nations.

Admiral Giuseppe Berutti Bergotto, Chief of the Italian Navy, visited INS Sudarshini and interacted with the ship’s crew and trainees. He was briefed on the ship’s voyage and training activities. The Commanding Officer, INS Sudarshini, called on Rear Admiral Alberto Tarabotto, Commandant, Italian Naval Academy, and shared experiences from the ongoing expedition. Interactions were also held with Mr Luca Salvetti, Mayor of Livorno, and Mr Edoardo Lombardi, Vice Prefect of Livorno.

As part of the training exchanges, Indian sea trainees visited ITS Virginio Fasan and the Italian Naval Academy, while Italian naval personnel visited INS Sudarshini, fostering professional cooperation and mutual understanding. A deck reception was hosted onboard, attended by senior Italian naval officers, local authorities, diplomatic representatives and distinguished guests.

As INS Sudarshini continues her voyage as part of Lokayan 2026, she carries forward the spirit of maritime partnership and the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurated the ‘Ganesh Gyanarthi Exhibition’ organised by the Asiatic Society of Mumbai in Mumbai today. On this occasion, Chief Minister of Maharashtra Shri Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Eknath Shinde, and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai Dr. Vinay Sahasrabuddhe, along with several other dignitaries were present.

 

Addressing the programme, Shri Amit Shah said that he has come to the Asiatic Society not as the Home Minister, but as a participant in the movement to carry forward the Indian knowledge tradition for thousands of years. Shri Shah expressed confidence that the Asiatic Society of Mumbai will become a bearer of the Indian knowledge tradition and spread it across the country.

 

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that a nation which cannot protect its smriti, history, values, language, records and traditions, no matter how powerful it may be, does not take long to decline; and a nation which protects its smriti, history, traditions, values, records, language and grammar, no matter for how many years it remains enslaved, cannot truly be enslaved by anyone. He said that many forces attempted to erase India’s radiant knowledge, which stood ready to guide the world, but they could not succeed. Shri Shah said that the library of Nalanda can be burned; it can be reduced to ashes with such intensity that smoke rises for months, but the knowledge that has settled in people’s minds in the form of Shruti and Smriti cannot be destroyed by anyone.

 

Shri Amit Shah said that it is the culture of our country that when we are defeated, we move forward with patience; and when we are victorious, we try to integrate those whom we have conquered into our tradition without destroying their memories. He said that true knowledge is never held hostage by any ideology. Knowledge itself is an ideology; if it is bound in any way, the very meaning of knowledge changes. Shri Shah said that knowledge should be free, uninhibited, and its proclamation should also be free and uninhibited. Therefore, instead of getting entangled in who founded the Asiatic Society and for what purpose, we should look at how the knowledge and collections that lie before us today can be used in the creation of a great India.

 

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that to understand the Asiatic Society, one must also understand the term ‘Indology’. Numismatics, epigraphy, morphology, history, archaeology, linguistics, philosophy, literature, theology and grammar — all these together constitute Indology. Its purpose was not the same as that of the Indian knowledge tradition, whose goal is the welfare of the world and the universe. At that time, its objective was to understand the systems here so as to rule over the people of this land for a long period. Shri Shah said that when an external power studies a civilisation, it either studies it or defines it. There is a fundamental difference between the two. When one studies it, one also accepts it and changes oneself. But when one defines it, the question of what the objective of that definition is becomes extremely important. He said that after the term Indology came into existence, this danger remained constant in the initial years.

 

Shri Amit Shah said that India’s knowledge was not being written in India’s voice. It was being written in the language of the colonial perspective, whose purpose was to create a collective inferiority complex within society and to diminish the self-confidence of our people. He said that when the people’s self-confidence is low, resistance to long-term slavery does not arise. The Home Minister said that the interpretation of the capital of knowledge was also done from that viewpoint, but today the country has become independent. More than eighty years of independence have passed. The government has changed, the committee of the Asiatic Society has also changed, and now there is confidence that this storehouse of knowledge will be used for the welfare of the universe, the world and the country, and ensuring this is the responsibility of the institution’s new committee. Shri Shah said that by understanding the objectives of the Indian knowledge tradition, it must be seen how this knowledge can spread across the country and the entire world and gain acceptance. He said that based on the works of Bharat Ratna Pandit Pandurang Vaman Kane, ‘Kane Samagra’ should be compiled and every single word of it prepared for the coming generation, so that a new generation is built. He said that many such treasures exist in this institution.

Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the British had intertwined knowledge and power with each other. Our task is to completely separate knowledge and power, so that power is created on the basis of knowledge, and the country is run on that very basis. Creating such a system is the work of the Asiatic Society. He said that it is often said in the country that history is being erased. Shri Shah said that he does not agree with those scholars. The process of decolonisation is not the erasure of history. It means placing history before the people once again in a complete, authentic manner and from an Indian perspective. This is decolonisation, and it must happen. Decolonisation does not mean erasure. Decolonisation means placing the truth before the world for the welfare of the world. Today we have moved towards decolonisation. He said that the Asiatic Society of Mumbai has illustrations of the Mahabharata, the Jain Kalpasutra, and such rare Buddhist texts that should have come out long ago.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that Maharashtra is the land of the Saraswats. The primacy and importance of Saraswati are already inherent in the energy of this land. He said that the new team of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai is expected to expand the storehouse of knowledge that lies here. This expansion should take place from three perspectives. He said that the Asiatic Society should expand and the manuscripts available here should be fully linked with the Gyan Bharatam National Manuscript Mission launched by the Government of India. The Asiatic Society should explore the possibility of running a campaign to collect ancestral documents from villages across Maharashtra and from the homes of scholars, and linking them with the Gyan Bharatam Manuscript Survey. He said that research arrangements under the Gyan Bharatam National Manuscript Mission should be considered for all the departments associated with the manuscripts present here. Shri Shah said that research is essential on the vast knowledge contained in the manuscripts. These hold the power to take the country forward. He said that in the first informal meeting of the Gyan Bharatam Manuscript Mission, a Jain monk had said that the seed to make India the best in the world in economic and defence terms is contained in these very manuscripts. Arrangements for research on this must be made.

 

Shri Amit Shah said that he has told Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis to empower the Society. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India is providing every possible support and cooperation to the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and will continue to do so in the future. Shri Shah said that all such institutions existing in every village, every town and every state of the country should be linked with the Asiatic Society of Mumbai to create a shared repository of knowledge, so that it becomes available to students, researchers and scholars across the entire country.

Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister meets the Vice President of Uganda on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 5:13PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi held a warm and productive bilateral meeting today with H.E. Jessica Rose Epel Alupo, Vice President of the Republic of Uganda, on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.

The two leaders reviewed bilateral ties between India and Uganda. They emphasized on the need to enhance cooperation in key priority areas through technology partnerships, capacity building, knowledge sharing, investment facilitation, and private-sector collaboration between the two countries. They also underlined that the development partnership between India and Uganda is a source of strength for both countries. Prime Minister reaffirmed India’s support to Uganda’s ‘Vision 2040’ for a transformed and prosperous Uganda. 2309719.title: India world's largest Vaccine producer and global supplier by volume: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh
2309719.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
India world's largest Vaccine producer and global supplier by volume: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh
India’s Diverse Disease Landscape Offers Unique Advantage for Vaccine Research and Epidemic Preparedness: Dr Jitendra Singh
India has moved far beyond the limitations of a decade ago in epidemic preparedness and is capable of contributing to the world’s preparedness for future pandemics: Dr Jitendra Singh
India Can Contribute to the Global Repository of Biomedical Solutions for Emerging Health Threats: Dr Jitendra Singh
India-CEPI Partnership Enters New Phase with Focus on Next-Generation Vaccines and Global Health Security: Dr Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 3:23PM by PIB Delhi

India has in recent years, emerged as the world's largest Vaccine producer and global supplier by volume , while India’s diverse disease landscape, combined with its expanding scientific capabilities, provides a unique platform for Vaccine research, epidemic preparedness and the development of biomedical solutions for global health, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, said today.

The Minister said, India has moved far beyond the limitations of a decade ago in epidemic preparedness and has built a vibrant bioeconomy, strong vaccine development capabilities and a scientific ecosystem capable of contributing to the world’s preparedness for future epidemics and pandemics.

Dr. Jitendra Singh was speaking at a High-Level Evening Reception for the "Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations" (CEPI) Board and Investors Council, jointly hosted by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India, and the CEPI at India International Centre, New Delhi. The reception brought together CEPI’s leadership, Board and Investors Council members, policymakers, scientists, industry representatives and other stakeholders engaged in vaccine development and epidemic preparedness. The CEPI Board and Investors Council meetings in New Delhi come a decade after the previous governance meeting was held in India, reflecting the depth of the India-CEPI partnership.

Congratulating CEPI and its partners on the occasion, Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s association with CEPI goes back to its formative years, with India as a founding member and a long-standing strategic partner. He also acknowledged the contribution of scientists and institutions that have helped build India’s vaccine and biomedical capabilities, including the teams led by senior scientific leaders such as Dr. Rajesh Gokhale, and the wider scientific fraternity.

The Minister said the progress made by India in the last decade represents a significant transformation in both epidemic preparedness and biotechnology. He said the country is today a vibrant bioeconomy and its capabilities can no longer be viewed only through the prism of vaccine manufacturing. India has moved into advanced vaccine technologies and complex biological products, supported by domestic research, manufacturing and clinical capabilities.

India’s bioeconomy reached USD 195.3 billion in 2025, recording 18 per cent year-on-year growth, while the country’s biotech startup ecosystem expanded to 11,855 startups, including 1,780 new startups added in 2025 alone. The biopharma sector accounts for nearly 30 per cent of India’s bioeconomy.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s transformation is particularly visible in the vaccine sector. From being known primarily for affordable vaccine manufacturing, India has developed capabilities across the value chain, from research and innovation to advanced biologics development and large-scale manufacturing. India supplies vaccines to more than 100 countries, accounts for nearly 60 per cent of global vaccine production and meets more than 65 per cent of WHO’s routine immunization requirements.

Recalling the COVID-19 experience, he said India not only developed vaccines in a remarkably short period but also extended them to other countries and partners. This journey, he said, has contributed to a significant change in the global perception of India’s scientific and technological capabilities.

The Minister said the country’s strength lies not merely in its manufacturing scale but also in the unique scientific opportunities created by India’s heterogeneous disease landscape. India continues to face a wide spectrum of communicable diseases while simultaneously dealing with the growing burden of non-communicable and metabolic disorders. This creates a dual challenge for preparedness, but also provides a rich scientific environment for understanding pathogens, disease patterns and interactions between infectious and metabolic conditions.

 

Dr. Jitendra Singh recalled that international researchers had historically come to India to study viruses, bacteria and diseases that were not readily found in their own countries. The same diversity, he said, can now become a strategic scientific advantage for India as it builds modern capabilities in pathogen research, vaccine development and epidemic preparedness.

“India provides such a fascinating research area” because of the combination of the diversity of microbes present in the country and the depth of scientific talent available to study them, Dr. Singh said. He said the country has an opportunity to contribute not only to its own preparedness but also to enriching the global repository of knowledge and biomedical solutions.

The DBT-BIRAC-CEPI partnership provides an important platform for translating this scientific potential into vaccines and other biomedical interventions. DBT and BIRAC have been working with CEPI under a tripartite engagement strategy aimed at strengthening preparedness for future epidemics and pandemics and advancing India’s R&D capabilities in vaccines for emerging infectious diseases. The engagement strategy, first executed in October 2019, was renewed in September 2025 for another five years.

The India-centric CEPI Mission, Ind-CEPI, implemented by BRIC-THSTI and BIRAC, has already delivered important outcomes. These include India’s first mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, GEMCOVAC-19, which received Emergency Use Authorisation; an inactivated Chikungunya vaccine candidate currently undergoing Phase II/III trials; and Multivalent Self-assembled Nanocage technology-based vaccine candidates for Monkeypox and pan-sarbecoviruses, which are at an advanced pre-clinical stage.

The partnership has also created shared infrastructure with global relevance. The BRIC-THSTI Bioassay Laboratory has been recognised as one of CEPI’s 17 centralised network laboratories and has supported eight vaccine candidates at different stages, from pre-clinical development to Phase III efficacy trials, for developers in India and several other countries. More than one lakh samples have been tested by the laboratory for vaccine development. BRIC-THSTI’s animal facility has also become part of CEPI’s pre-clinical network.

Capacity building has formed another important part of the engagement. BRIC-THSTI, in collaboration with CEPI, has conducted advanced Vaccinology Courses, while the PACT programme has provided online training to more than 2,400 participants from 14 friendly and neighbouring countries, strengthening clinical trial capabilities across the region.

The Minister said the next phase of cooperation must build on these achievements and translate India’s scientific strengths into greater global health impact. The Ind-CEPI Mission is expected to further strengthen India’s biomedical intervention development ecosystem through universal and pan-pathogen vaccine development, advanced biomanufacturing capabilities and wider national and global collaborative networks.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said India is now in a position to contribute its scientific capabilities, research infrastructure and disease diversity to a global preparedness architecture, while simultaneously strengthening its own capacity to respond rapidly to emerging health threats. The convergence of cutting-edge science, scalable manufacturing and international partnerships, he said, can help India move from preparedness for individual outbreaks towards sustained leadership in next-generation vaccines and biomedical interventions.

The Minister also called for greater engagement across government, academia, industry and international partners so that scientific capabilities can be converted into deployable solutions. He said the purpose of such gatherings was not merely to exchange views but to build meaningful fellowship and collaboration that could take the shared objective of epidemic preparedness forward.

The reception thus marked a significant moment in the India-CEPI partnership, bringing the organisation’s Board and Investors Council to New Delhi after a decade and providing a platform to carry forward cooperation in vaccine innovation, epidemic preparedness and global health security.

2309713.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will address the inaugural session of Hindi Diwas 2026 and the 6th All India Official Language Conference in Mumbai on Monday, 14 September
Inspired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Department of Official Language under MHA has been organizing All India Official Language Conferences annually since 2021
During the inaugural session of two-day event, Union Home Minister will present the ‘Rajbhasha Gaurav’ and ‘Rajbhasha Kirti’ awards for the year 2025–26
Institutions and individuals who have undertaken outstanding work and made noteworthy contributions in the field of Official Language will be honoured with these awards

Several important books and publications will also be launched during the inaugural session and other sessions; these include a special commemorative issue of the Department of Official Language’s journal ‘Rajbhasha Bharati’, centred on ‘Vande Mataram’
A special session will be held at the Conference on the role of Town Official Language Implementation Committees (TOLICs/NARAKAS)
A special exhibition will be organized at the venue, featuring a total of 32 stalls set up by various institutions, organizations, banks, and ministries
The event will also highlight the vibrant relationship of Hindi with Maharashtra’s rich linguistic, cultural and literary traditions
The 6th All India Official Language Conference will provide an opportunity to further strengthen coordination, dialogue and partnership among all Indian languages along with Hindi
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 2:48PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will address the inaugural session of Hindi Diwas 2026 and the 6th All India Official Language Conference in Mumbai on Monday, 14 September. On this occasion, the Chief Minister of Maharashtra, both Deputy Chief Ministers, several Members of Parliament, distinguished guests from various fields, scholars, litterateurs, educationists, and senior officials from various departments and ministries of the Central Government will also be present. This event will also highlight the vibrant relationship of Hindi with Maharashtra’s rich linguistic, cultural, and literary traditions.

Inspired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and under the able guidance of Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, the Department of Official Language of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has been organizing All India Official Language Conferences every year since 2021. This journey, which began from Varanasi, has reached Navi Mumbai in Maharashtra this year, passing through Surat, Pune, New Delhi and Gandhinagar.

During the inaugural session of the two-day programme, the ‘Rajbhasha Gaurav’ and ‘Rajbhasha Kirti’ Awards for the year 2025–26 will be presented by the Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah. The institutions and individuals who have undertaken outstanding work and made noteworthy contributions in the field of Official Language will be honoured with these awards.

Several important books and publications will also be launched during the inaugural session and other sessions. These include a special commemorative issue of the Department of Official Language’s journal ‘Rajbhasha Bharati’, centred on the National Song ‘Vande Mataram’; ‘Bharatiya Gyan Tantra: Srot aur Swaroop’; ‘Shiv Anadi Hain, Anant Hain’; and ‘Andheron Se Ujalon Tak’, a compilation of writings by prison inmates. These publications bring forth diverse dimensions of Indian culture, knowledge tradition, literature and creative expression. Books and journals of several other organisations and institutions will also be launched.

A special attraction of this year’s Conference will be a special discussion session centred on the National Song ‘Vande Mataram’. ‘Vande Mataram’ has not merely been a song, but has been a powerful expression of India’s consciousness of freedom, national self-respect and dedication towards the motherland. In this special session, renowned playback singer Shri Hariharan, senior journalist and writer Shri Nilesh Mishra, and Shri Akhilesh Mishra, who is studying ‘Vande Mataram’, will participate in the discussion. In addition, researcher of ‘Vande Mataram’, Shri Milind Prabhakar Sabnis, will shed light on the historical, literary and cultural aspects of this National Song in another session. Shri Joydeep Chattopadhyay will also have a special presence at the programme. He is a fifth-generation descendant of Shri Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, the author of ‘Vande Mataram’. His presence will lend special historical and emotional significance to this event. Through these sessions, deliberations will be held on how ‘Vande Mataram’ gave voice to national consciousness in the Indian public mind and how its relevance has continued from the freedom movement to the present day.

A special session will also be organised at the Conference on the role of Town Official Language Implementation Committees (TOLICs/NARAKAS). NARAKAS is a strong and empowered unit that takes forward the implementation of Official Language Hindi at the grassroots level. This session will discuss and deliberate upon the work and achievements of NARAKAS and its role in Official Language implementation, and NARAKAS performing outstanding work will also be honoured.

In a special session to be held after the lunch break on 15 September, renowned lyricist and writer Shri Manoj Muntashir will be present. Shri Muntashir, who is particularly popular for his songs imbued with the spirit of patriotism and love for the nation, will share his thoughts on this occasion. This session will further enrich the cultural and emotional dignity of the Conference. Thereafter, a grand cultural programme will be organised by the Government of Maharashtra, in which diverse glimpses of Maharashtra’s rich cultural and artistic traditions will be witnessed.

A special exhibition is also being organised at the Conference venue, in which stalls will be put up by various institutions, organisations, banks and ministries. A total of 32 stalls, including two special stalls of the Government of Maharashtra, and stalls of the Department of Official Language and the Publications Division, will be set up at the exhibition venue. Through these stalls, the work, publications, initiatives and achievements of various institutions relating to Hindi and Indian languages will be displayed.

During the two-day Conference, deliberations will be held on various subjects related to the development of Hindi as the Official Language, people’s language and link language; its coordination with Indian languages; technology and language; translation; literature; and the wider dissemination of Hindi.

The Article 343 of the Constitution provides for Hindi in Devanagari script as the Official Language of the Union, while Article 351 places upon the Union the responsibility for the promotion, development and enrichment of Hindi. The Department of Official Language is continuously working towards the discharge of these constitutional responsibilities. In this sequence, the Sixth All India Official Language Conference being organised will provide an opportunity to further strengthen coordination, dialogue and partnership among all Indian languages along with Hindi.

2309702.title: India to host World Circular Economy Forum 2026, themed 'Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity', at Gandhinagar during 15th - 18th September, 2026
2309702.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2309702.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India to host World Circular Economy Forum 2026, themed 'Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity', at Gandhinagar during 15th - 18th September, 2026
Forum a Global Platform for Cross-sectoral Partnerships to facilitate Circular Finance and advancing Innovation for Circularity
2,000+ Stakeholders from 65+ Countries to participate; 125+ exhibitors to showcase Circularity Solutions at the International Expo
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 2:22PM by PIB Delhi

India would host the World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF) 2026, at Gandhinagar (Gujarat) on 15th-18th September, 2026. A First for South Asia, the forum would be jointly inaugurated on the 15th by Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, and Chief Minister of Gujarat, Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel. The forum would be organised under the theme 'Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity'. Other dignitaries to grace the inaugural session would include Minister for Forest, Environment and Climate Change (Gujarat), Shri Arjunbhai Modhwadia; Ambassador of Finland to India, H.E. Mr. Mikko Kivikoski; Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate (Netherlands), Ms. Marieke Spijkerboer, along with senior officials from the Government of India and Government of Gujarat.

Circularity focuses on reusing, refurbishing and recycling existing materials and products and looping them back into the economy as valuable resources. Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India is leading a major transformation in environmental governance, moving toward a modern circular economy. The event is being jointly organized by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) of India, the Finnish Innovation Fund Sitra, Government of Finland, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC), Government of India, Government of Gujarat and Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB).

The objective of WCEF 2026 is to showcase India’s initiatives for promoting circularity and enhancing international cooperation. The event would witness participation of over 2000 cross-sectoral stakeholders from 65+ countries, including business leaders, entrepreneurs, innovators, researchers, policymakers, academicians, changemakers and others. The forum will enable global collaboration and greater engagement with the Global South; facilitate mobilising of circular finance and private-sector investment; encourage policy dialogue and cross-sectoral partnerships; while advancing innovation, digitalisation and technology for circularity.

On 15th–16th September 2026, the forum would feature 4 plenaries and 16 parallel thematic sessions on application of AI, employment potential, energy production, finance, governance, sustainable products, industrial solutions, start-up ecosystem and youth leadership. Further at the event, an expo featuring 125+ national and international exhibitors would showcase practical circular solutions developed by start-ups and investment-ready innovations.

On the sidelines of WCEF, the Board of 10 Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Consumption and Production Patterns (10 YFP) would hold its in person meeting, on 15th September at Gandhinagar. India has recently assumed the role of Co-Chair of 10 YFP Board, reflecting its long standing leadership in promoting sustainable consumption and production. On 17th–18th September 2026, global collaborators will independently organize 80 accelerator sessions online/hybrid and in person at Gandhinagar and other locations worldwide.

The closing ceremony would be graced by the presence of Minister for Forests, Environment and Climate Change (Gujarat), Shri Arjunbhai Devabhai Modhwadia. Dignitaries expected on the occasion would include Minister of Climate and the Environment (Finland), Ms. Sari Multala; Minister of State for Forests and Environment, Climate Change (Gujarat), Shri Pravinbhai Mali; Director, International Programmes, SITRA, Mr. Kristo Lehtonen, along with senior government officials from the Government of India and the Government of Gujarat. The ceremony will conclude with a formal handover to the next host by the Director, International Programme of SITRA, with a message that embracing circular economy principles, the world can shape a global economy that is more sustainable, resilient and prosperous.
