2309696.title: Coal Supply to Punjab Power Plants Remains Adequate; Timely Lifting from CIL and Higher Captive Coal Utilisation Key to Sustained Generation
2309696.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
Coal Supply to Punjab Power Plants Remains Adequate; Timely Lifting from CIL and Higher Captive Coal Utilisation Key to Sustained Generation
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 2:13PM by PIB Delhi

Media reports today, including one titled “Punjab power crisis deepens as 14-hour cuts hit factories, farms,” have attributed reduced power generation at Punjab's thermal plants towards plant outages and inadequate coal supply. The Ministry of Coal clarifies that this does not present the complete picture. Adequate coal has been made available to Punjab's power plants, and Coal India Limited (CIL) remains fully committed to ensuring uninterrupted coal supply for power generation across the country, including in Punjab.

The Central Government has already taken steps to enable coal movement to Punjab's Independent Power Plants (IPPs) from PSPCL's captive mines. Higher utilisation of PSPCL's own plants, monitoring breakdowns at IPPs, together with timely lifting of coal already offered by CIL subsidiaries, would help optimise power generation and address the State's requirements.

Central Government and CIL's Support to Punjab's Coal Supply Chain

The Central Government has proactively facilitated coal movement to IPPs in Punjab since the commencement of captive mine production:

  • Supply of coal from PSPCL's captive Pachhwara Central Coal Mine to IPPs has been enabled, subject to fulfilment of the statutory payment obligation to the State of Jharkhand.
  • Utilisation of coal from the Pachhwara Central Coal Mine by IPPs not owned by PSPCL,  including Nabha Power Limited (Rajpura) and Talwandi Sabo Power Limited (Mansa) is already permitted up to 50% of annual production, after meeting the requirements of Specified End Use Plants.

CIL supply to Punjab's IPPs remains adequate

Against NPL's average consumption of around 4.3 rakes/day over the last three days, rake supply has averaged around 5 rakes/day; against TSPL's consumption of around 3.8 rakes/day, supply has averaged around 5 rakes/day. Through September 2026 so far, average supply has been around 4.9 rakes/day for NPL and 4.1 rakes/day for TSPL, which is higher than the average consumption of these IPPs.

Punjab needs to Improve Offtake from Captive Mines of PSPCL

At the Pachhwara Central mine of PSPCL, for the period April 2026 to 11.09.2026, production stands at 83.67% of the annual target, while despatch stands at only 68.44% of the target. This gap points to a build-up of unevacuated stock at the mine of around 3.21 lakh tonnes, which the State should evacuate to generate more power at PSPCL's own plants.

Lower PLF at PSPCL's Plants and Breakdowns at IPPs

PSPCL operates three thermal power plants i.e., Guru Hargobind TPS (Lehra Mohabbat), Goindwal Sahib TPP, and Ropar TPS with a combined capacity of 2,300 MW. As on 11.09.2026, coal stock at PSPCL's plants stood at around 114% of the normative requirement, reflecting more than adequate coal availability.

Despite this comfortable stock position, the tentative Plant Load Factor (PLF) of PSPCL's plants during September 2026 was only around 59%. The low generation during the month therefore cannot be attributed to inadequate coal availability at the plant end.

Separately, breakdowns have been reported at IPP power plants, which the State of Punjab may wish to closely monitor to sustain power generation.

IPPs Need to Improve Lifting of Coal Already Offered by CIL

CIL subsidiaries have proactively offered additional coal to Punjab-based IPPs; however, booking and lifting have remained below the quantities offered:

  • CCL offered 5.0 lakh tonnes (LT) of coal to NPL and TSPL on 30.03.2026 under the RCR mode, against which around 4.1 LT has been booked and 3.2 LT lifted so far.
  • BCCL offered 3.5 LT of coal to NPL, against which around 1.7 LT has been booked and 1.1 LT lifted so far.
  • Considering the surge in power demand, CIL has additionally allocated 2.30 LT of coal to NPL from BCCL and 3.0 LT to TSPL from CCL under the Flexibility Policy in Q2; lifting against these allocations is yet to commence.

Thus, additional coal has continued to be made available to Punjab-based IPPs, and timely lifting of the allocated/offered coal would be important for augmenting coal availability at the plant end.

While CIL and its subsidiaries are taking measures to augment coal availability through RCR, the Flexibility Policy and additional rail-based arrangements, timely booking and lifting of coal already offered by CIL along with optimal utilisation of available rake supply, remains critical for improving coal receipts at NPL and TSPL.

 

The Ministry of Coal and Coal India Limited remain committed to supplying coal to the State of Punjab under existing fuel supply arrangements, covering PSPCL as well as all IPPs in the State. Timely lifting of coal by IPPs, improved offtake from PSPCL's own captive mines, and better generation performance at PSPCL's plants are equally important for optimising power generation in Punjab.

2309693.title: Defence Secretary meets Vietnam’s Deputy Minister of National Defence on the sidelines of BRICS Summit
2309693.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Defence Secretary meets Vietnam’s Deputy Minister of National Defence on the sidelines of BRICS Summit
India and Vietnam reaffirm commitment to stronger maritime & defence ties for regional security
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 1:54PM by PIB Delhi

Following the recent high-level bilateral meeting between the Prime Ministers of India and Vietnam on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh held a meeting with the Deputy Minister of National Defence of Vietnam Senior Lieutenant General Nguyen Truong Thang in New Delhi on September 13, 2026. The meeting focused on strengthening the bonds of friendship, advancing regional security, and deepening the bilateral Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

The discussions centered on accelerating joint initiatives, technology sharing and defence industrial collaboration. The two sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to expanding maritime and defence ties to ensure a peaceful, stable, and rule-based regional security architecture.

India and Vietnam strongly emphasised the value of close coordination in multilateral fora to address complex security dynamics. Specifically, they highlighted the importance of active engagement under the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting Plus (ADMM-Plus) construct.

Both sides reaffirmed their joint commitment to enhancing practical defence cooperation through ASEAN-led mechanisms, noting that collaborative platforms like the ADMM-Plus Experts' Working Groups are vital for maintaining regional stability and building collective security architectures in the Indo-Pacific. They agreed on the scheduled conduct of the next Defence Policy Dialogue to be hosted in India on the sidelines of Aero India 2027.

The interaction underscores the growing momentum in defence ties between India and Vietnam, building directly on the strategic vision set forth by both Prime Ministers at the BRICS summit.

2309690.title: CAZRI Moth Bean Varieties Demonstrate Remarkable Resilience During El Niño Year
2309690.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
CAZRI Moth Bean Varieties Demonstrate Remarkable Resilience During El Niño Year
CAZRI Moth Bean Varieties Withstand 35-Day Dry Spell During Kharif 2026
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 1:40PM by PIB Delhi

Moth bean, one of the most important pulse crops of the hot arid regions of western Rajasthan, is cultivated over nearly 10 lakh hectares. However, its productivity remains low at around 350 kg per hectare, primarily due to low, erratic and uncertain rainfall of 150–250 mm, prolonged dry spells of 20–30 days and limited availability of soil moisture. Under such challenging conditions, the ability of a variety to withstand moisture stress, maintain growth and continue reproductive development is critical for sustaining crop production.

 

Addressing these challenges, the ICAR–Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI), Jodhpur, has undertaken long-term moth bean breeding and genetic improvement programmes aimed at developing varieties with developmental plasticity, enhanced stress resilience and high yield potential suited to the harsh and unpredictable conditions of the arid region. In the last three years, four varieties—CAZRI Moth-4, CAZRI Moth-5, CAZRI Moth-6 and CAZRI Moth-7—have been released. Their performance during the current El Niño year (Kharif 2026) has demonstrated remarkable field-level resilience, particularly under a prolonged moisture stress period of around 35 days.

 

During the crop growth period from 10 July to 2 September 2026, cumulative pan evaporation was around 317 mm. Rainfall ceased after the rainfall event of 3 August 2026, resulting in a prolonged rainless period during the subsequent crop growth and reproductive stages. During the 35-day dry spell from 3 August to 7 September 2026, cumulative pan evaporation was around 180 mm. The crop received rainfall mainly during the early stages of establishment and growth. Early canopy development, soil binding and moisture retention in the rhizosphere supported crop establishment and helped the plants withstand the prolonged dry spell. Surface soil moisture at 0–10 cm depth was around 15–16 per cent (v/v) until 2 August 2026, when the last significant rainfall of 86 mm was received. Thereafter, a dry spell of more than one month, accompanied by three to four scattered rainfall events of less than 2.5 mm each, reduced surface soil moisture to around 5–6 per cent. At the 10–40 cm subsurface layer, soil moisture declined from around 23 per cent to 16 per cent, which continued to contribute to meeting the crop’s water requirement.

The field performance of the CAZRI varieties was supported by appropriate crop management practices, including timely sowing with the onset of the monsoon in July, optimum plant geometry of 45 × 10 cm, mechanical interculture operations at 20 days after sowing for moisture conservation, mechanical weed management along with manual spot weeding and effective canopy development for efficient utilisation of available soil moisture. The experimental fields had poor fertility conditions, with organic carbon content of 0.13–0.18 per cent, soil pH of 7.9–8.1, available nitrogen of 90–100 kg per hectare, available phosphorus of 10–15 kg per hectare and available potassium of 250–260 kg per hectare.

 

The four recently developed CAZRI moth bean varieties are also being multiplied for seed production. Seed production is currently being undertaken over seven hectares at the CAZRI Research Farm to meet the Saathi Portal-indented seed requirement of 23.32 quintals for 2026. In 2025, the seed indented through the Saathi Portal for all four varieties was 63.2 quintals. One quintal of breeder seed can produce around 1,000–1,400 quintals of certified seed and, when properly multiplied and marketed as certified seed, can facilitate cultivation over around 10,000 hectares. Even at 50 per cent of this potential, wider adoption of these varieties in Rajasthan could cover around 25 per cent of the total moth bean area. The seed is being multiplied by Rajasthan State Seeds Corporation, National Seeds Corporation and selected private players.

The performance of these varieties was particularly significant as the prolonged moisture deficit coincided with flowering, pod formation and reproductive development. Despite the extended period without substantial rainfall, the varieties maintained a green appearance, good growth and profuse pod development at around 55 days after sowing. Developed through more than a decade of systematic moth bean breeding and genetic improvement at CAZRI, these varieties have been selected with emphasis on adaptation to the harsh and unpredictable arid environment of western Rajasthan. Their ability to maintain active vegetative growth and reproductive development during the prolonged rainless period provides an important field-level indication of their genetic potential and adaptability to moisture-stress conditions.

 

An important adaptation characteristic of these varieties is developmental plasticity. The varieties begin flowering at approximately 30 days after sowing and possess the ability to adjust their growth and maturity according to the availability of soil moisture. Such flexibility is particularly valuable in western Rajasthan, where rainfall varies considerably in amount, timing and distribution. The ability to progress rapidly towards reproductive development while efficiently utilising available soil moisture, combined with appropriate crop management, provides an important adaptation advantage for moth bean cultivation under rainfed arid conditions.

 

Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, ICAR, said that moth bean is a unique crop of the Thar Desert wherein these highly climate-resilient moth bean varieties of CAZRI could play an important role in making the Thar Desert more prosperous and creating new income opportunities for farmers and contributing to achieving self-reliance on pulses. He said that the ability of these varieties to maintain growth and pod development during a prolonged period without rainfall demonstrates the potential of genetic improvement as an important component of climate-resilient agriculture. At the same time, he emphasised that a package of best management practices such as optimum plant population, timely sowing, weed management and moisture-conservation practices are essential for enabling varieties to realise their genetic potential under stress conditions.

*****

2309685.title: From Sanitation Worker to Self-Reliance: Shri Harish Chandra Parbat’s Journey through Mechanised Sanitation
2309685.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Sanitation Worker to Self-Reliance: Shri Harish Chandra Parbat’s Journey through Mechanised Sanitation
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 1:17PM by PIB Delhi

Access to mechanised sanitation equipment and financial assistance can help sanitation professionals strengthen their livelihoods and meet their family responsibilities. Shri Harish Chandra Parbat’s journey reflects how support for livelihood development can improve earning opportunities and enable the next generation to pursue higher education.

Shri Harish Chandra Parbat, a 46-year-old sanitation professional originally from Siwan district, Bihar, has strengthened his livelihood through assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY).

Belonging to the OBC/Goswami community and educated up to the twelfth standard, he now operates a tractor-cum-suction machine for sanitation service activities under Ghaziabad Municipal Corporation in the Sahibabad Industrial Area.

In search of employment and a more secure future, Shri Parbat migrated to Delhi in 2015. He worked in sanitation-related activities and gradually gained practical experience in sewer and septic tank operations. From 2015 to 2020, he continued working in these services, but his earnings remained largely committed to everyday household needs.

His earlier monthly income of approximately ₹13,000–₹14,000 made it difficult to manage household expenditure, rental costs and his children’s educational needs. He also had the responsibility of financially supporting his mother, who resides in Siwan, Bihar. Limited resources left little scope for savings or investment in livelihood growth.

Despite these challenges, Shri Parbat remained determined to improve his family’s living standards. He believed that education could create a better future for his children and aspired to establish a stable livelihood that would enable them to pursue higher studies and build successful careers.

Financial assistance released on 26 November 2021 enabled him to procure a tractor-cum-suction machine. Against a total project cost of ₹9,75,400, he received a loan of ₹6,06,550 and an upfront capital subsidy of ₹3,68,850. This support helped him strengthen his sanitation service operations and improve his earning capacity.

 

With access to mechanised equipment, Shri Parbat’s reported monthly earnings increased to approximately ₹40,000–₹45,000. The improvement enabled him to better meet his family responsibilities and invest in his children’s education. In 2022, he brought his wife and children to Delhi, allowing the family to live together and pursue improved educational opportunities.

Today, his eldest son is pursuing the final year of graduation, his second son is studying in the second year of B.Tech, and his daughter is pursuing the first year of B.Tech. All three children are studying in Delhi. His wife, a homemaker, manages household responsibilities.

Shri Parbat continues to meet monthly rent of approximately ₹12,000 and a loan instalment of ₹13,500, alongside educational and household expenses. He also sends approximately ₹3,000 each month to support his mother in Siwan. As on 27 May 2026, his remaining loan amount stood at ₹1,27,490. While these commitments limit his savings, his improved earnings have strengthened his ability to support his family and continue repaying the loan.

Reflecting on his progress, Shri Parbat said, “The biggest achievement of my life is seeing my children pursuing higher education and moving towards a brighter future. Today, I am gradually repaying my loan and moving ahead with confidence and dignity.”

Shri Harish Chandra Parbat’s journey demonstrates the role of livelihood assistance and mechanised sanitation equipment in supporting economic self-reliance. His progress has strengthened his family’s financial position and created opportunities for all three of his children to pursue higher education.

2309682.title: From Financial Constraints to Doctoral Achievement: Dr. Moniya’s Journey through the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students
2309682.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Constraints to Doctoral Achievement: Dr. Moniya’s Journey through the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 12:54PM by PIB Delhi

For Dr. Moniya, completing a Ph.D. meant overcoming financial constraints and becoming the first person in her family to earn a doctoral degree. Support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) helped her sustain her research and achieve this milestone.

Dr. Moniya, a 29-year-old scholar from Kurukshetra, Haryana, successfully completed her Ph.D. with assistance under the NFSC Scheme. Her achievement reflects her perseverance through financial difficulties and the role of fellowship support in enabling her to continue doctoral research.

With an aspiration to become a scientist and undertake novel research in nano-biotechnology, Dr. Moniya was determined to pursue higher education. However, her family lacked sufficient financial resources to support her doctoral studies. Research expenses placed considerable pressure on her and caused concern within her family.

According to Dr. Moniya, limited support from her research supervisor added to these difficulties. She faced expenses for sample testing, stationery, laboratory equipment repairs and participation in conferences. She also reported experiencing caste discrimination and delays during her doctoral journey, making an already demanding period more difficult.

Despite these challenges, she continued working towards completing her Ph.D. Her ambition to undertake scientific research remained an important motivation, while her experiences during higher education also encouraged her to consider a future career in administration.

NFSC assistance began in March 2022. Dr. Moniya received more than Rs. 10 lakh through fellowship payments, House Rent Allowance (HRA) and contingency assistance. This support helped her meet expenses associated with chemicals, equipment, sample testing, conference fees, thesis printing and laboratory instrument repairs.

 

 

The assistance helped address the financial barriers affecting her doctoral work. By providing resources for research and academic participation, the fellowship enabled her to continue her studies and work towards completing her thesis.

 

With fellowship support, Dr. Moniya completed her Ph.D. and became the first doctoral degree holder in her family. Earning the title “Dr.” marked a significant personal achievement and a milestone for a family that had worried about the financial demands of her higher education.

Dr. Moniya is currently preparing for UPSC examinations, scientist recruitment examinations and assistant professor examinations. Alongside her interest in scientific research, she wishes to pursue a career in administration as she works towards her next professional opportunity.

Extending her gratitude to the Ministry’s support, Dr Moniya said, “NFSC support helped me complete my PhD and become the first doctoral degree holder in my family.”

Her journey demonstrates how fellowship assistance can help scholars overcome financial barriers to doctoral education. NFSC support helped Dr. Moniya complete her research and earn her degree, providing a foundation for her future academic and professional aspirations.

2309673.title: From Childhood Adversity to Recovery and Self-Reliance:  Rahul Llowang’s Journey under NAPDDR
2309673.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Childhood Adversity to Recovery and Self-Reliance: Rahul Llowang’s Journey under NAPDDR
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 12:38PM by PIB Delhi

Recovery can open pathways to renewed confidence, independence and a more stable life. Treatment, counselling and rehabilitation support can help individuals overcome substance dependency and rebuild their lives.

Rahul Llowang (name changed), a 27-year-old man from the Scheduled Tribe community in Tirap district, Arunachal Pradesh, received treatment and rehabilitation support under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) at the District De-Addiction Centre (DDAC) run by Care Me Home Welfare Society at Charju, Khonsa.

Today, Rahul is self-employed and has become more financially independent, moving towards a more stable and productive life.

Rahul’s childhood was marked by difficult family circumstances. The loss of his father at an early age left him without adequate care, guidance and emotional support. These challenges disrupted his education, which he could pursue only up to middle school. During this vulnerable period, he began using substances at the age of 11.

Limited family support and difficulties in finding acceptance within society added to his struggles. Despite these hardships, Rahul continued to aspire to a stable and disciplined life. He hoped to join the Indian Reserve Battalion (IRBN) and secure meaningful employment.

The connection with the DDAC run by Care Me Home Welfare Society at Charju, Khonsa, in Tirap district, proved a turning point. On 9 May 2024, Rahul received support under NAPDDR, including a highly subsidised treatment plan, counselling services and rehabilitation assistance.

The intervention helped Rahul overcome substance dependency, strengthen his personal skills and move towards a more stable life. Counselling and rehabilitation services supported his recovery and social reintegration, while community support and preventive interventions helped strengthen the rehabilitation process.

 

Rahul’s progress reflects the positive change that accessible treatment, counselling and community support can bring to a person’s life. His self-employment and greater financial independence mark meaningful steps towards self-reliance.

Expressing his joy and contentment, Rahul Llowang (name changed) said, “Treatment and counselling helped me overcome dependency and rebuild my life with confidence”.

Rahul’s journey highlights the role of NAPDDR-supported de-addiction services in helping individuals rebuild their lives with dignity and renewed hope. From a childhood shaped by loss and limited support, he is now moving towards greater stability and self-reliance.

2309671.title: Strengthening Welfare Healthcare Support And Dignified Living For Senior Citizens
2309671.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Strengthening Welfare Healthcare Support And Dignified Living For Senior Citizens
More Than 2.88 Lakh Senior Citizens Benefit From Essential Care And Support Services; 142 New Senior Citizen Homes Sanctioned
228 Camps Cover Over 4.91 Lakh Beneficiaries, With Around 23.93 Lakh Free Assistive Living Devices Distributed
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 12:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is continuously  taking measures to strengthen welfare, protection, healthcare support and dignified living for senior citizens. These efforts focus on expanding institutional care, providing essential services and improving access to assistive living devices for elderly persons.

Giving details, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant said that more than 2.88 lakh senior citizens have benefited from the provision of shelter, nutritious food, healthcare services, physiotherapy, recreation and other essential support facilities. These services support their daily needs and promote their physical well-being and quality of life.

He said that 142 new Senior Citizen Homes have been sanctioned across different parts of the country, to expand institutional care and support infrastructure adding the additional homes will strengthen access to care and essential support for elderly persons.

The Secretary added that to enhance accessibility and independent living, 228 camps were organised covering more than 4.91 lakh beneficiaries whileas around 23.93 lakh free assistive living devices were distributed. These included wheelchairs, hearing aids, walking sticks and spectacles for eligible senior citizens belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) categories and low-income groups supporting mobility, communication and participation in everyday activities, he added.

Shri Pant added that to further strengthen access to information, a Senior Citizen’s Welfare Portal was launched by the Hon’ble President of India as a one-stop solution for information dissemination that provides a common platform for accessing information related to senior citizens’ welfare.

The Secretary said that these measures reinforce the Ministry’s commitment to supporting senior citizens through accessible care, improved welfare infrastructure and assistance that enables them to lead dignified and independent lives.

*****

2309666.title: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Strengthens Safety Welfare and Dignity of Sanitation Workers
2309666.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Strengthens Safety Welfare and Dignity of Sanitation Workers
87,037 sewer and septic tank workers provided PPE kits; Rs 34.17 crore capital subsidy released to support procurement of sanitation vehicles
Waste pickers included under the scheme since June 2024; 3,78,547 profiled across urban and rural areas
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 12:14PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment is advancing measures for the welfare and dignity of sanitation workers through worker profiling, provision of protective equipment, health insurance coverage, financial assistance and strengthening of safety infrastructure.

Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment Shri Sudhansh Pant said that a total of 90,942 sewer and septic tank workers have been profiled, of whom 89,248 have been validated. He said that Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits have been provided to 87,037 workers, while 76,247 workers have been covered under various health insurance schemes that support safer working conditions and access to healthcare protection.

The Secretary said that to facilitate access to sanitation vehicles, an upfront capital subsidy of Rs 34.17 crore has been released to 983 sanitation workers for procurement of 364 vehicles. This assistance supports mechanised sanitation operations and livelihood opportunities for workers, he added.

Shri Pant said to further strengthen safety infrastructure, 753 safety devices have been dispatched to Emergency Response Sanitation Units (ERSUs) established in larger municipal corporations and districts.

He added that alongside financial and welfare support, 1,562 workshops on prevention of hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks have been conducted across the country.

The Secretary further said that the Scheme’s coverage was expanded in June 2024 to include waste pickers engaged in solid waste management in both urban and rural areas, extending welfare and safety support to this group of workers.

 

Shri Pant elaborated that a total of 3,78,547 waste pickers have been profiled, of whom 2,52,163 have been validated through e-KYC. He added that around 1,31,864 waste pickers have received PPE kits, while the data of 1,24,835 waste pickers has been processed for generation of Ayushman Cards.

Shri Pant exuded confidence that these measures reflect the Ministry’s efforts to strengthen occupational safety, improve access to welfare benefits and uphold the dignity of workers engaged in sanitation and solid waste management.

*********

2309664.title: Text of Prime Minister's opening address during the 18th BRICS Summit session: "Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Development"
2309664.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Text of Prime Minister's opening address during the 18th BRICS Summit session: "Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Development"
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 12:11PM by PIB Delhi

Your Highness,
Excellencies, 
नमस्कार।

ब्रिक्स के विस्तृत परिवार में आप सभी का हार्दिक स्वागत है।

आज यह सभागार अलग-अलग महाद्वीपों, संस्कृतियों और विकास यात्राओं को एक साथ जोड़ रहा है। यह ब्रिक्स की बढ़ती ताकत, आकर्षण और अभूतपूर्व विश्वास का प्रमाण है।

Friends,

भारत की अध्यक्षता में हमने सभी प्रयास Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation और Sustainability, इन चार स्तंभों पर केंद्रित किये हैं। मुझे खुशी है कि आप सबके सहयोग और समर्थन से हम अपने साझा vision को win-win सहयोग में बदल सके। 

आज विश्व में तनावों की संख्या लगातार बढ़ रही है, और सामान्य मानव के जीवन पर इसका बहुत negative प्रभाव भी हो रहा है, और व्यापक प्रभाव भी हो रहा है। 

महामारियों, climate disasters और supply-chain disruptions ने दिखाया है कि आज के interconnected world में कोई भी संकट एक क्षेत्र तक सीमित नहीं रहता। इसलिए हमने ब्रिक्स समूह में Resilience बढ़ाने पर विशेष बल दिया है। चुनौतियों को समय रहते पहचानना, उनके लिए तैयार रहना और तुरंत कार्रवाई करना भी उतना ही आवश्यक है। 

इसी सोच के साथ, infectious diseases के prevention और response के लिए BRICS Integrated Early Warning System पर सहमति बनी है। Disaster Management के लिए Early Warning Data Integration Guidelines तैयार की गई हैं। BRICS Logistics Supply Chain Cooperation Framework हमारी supply chains को अधिक reliable और resilient बनाने में सहायक होगा।

Friends,

Innovation के अंतर्गत BRICS Incubator Network हमारे start-ups और incubators को आपस में जोड़ेगा। Innovative और scalable solutions को बढ़ावा देने के लिए हमने BRICS Startup Innovation Fund का प्रस्ताव रखा है। 

BRICS Network on Digital Agriculture किसानों के लिए नई संभावनाएं तैयार करेगा। इसके माध्यम से AI, geospatial technology और Digital Public Infrastructure को किसानों की वास्तविक आवश्यकताओं से जोड़ा जाएगा।

Technology और Critical Minerals का weaponization हमारी साझा प्रगति में बाधा बन सकता है। इसलिए हमने technology के adoption में inclusivity पर बल दिया है। 

Friends,

भारत ने ब्रिक्स के मंच से मित्रता, सहभागिता और सहयोग को आगे बढ़ाया है। 

हमारा प्रयास रहा है कि ब्रिक्स cooperation केवल सरकारों तक सीमित न रहे। हमारे entrepreneurs, farmers, researchers, women, youth और सामान्य नागरिक भी इसके सक्रिय भागीदार बनें। 

हमने BRICS CONNECT के माध्यम से skills, employability, women in workforce, social security और capacity building को बढ़ावा दिया है। 

छोटे उद्यमों को knowledge, finance और नए markets से जोड़ने के लिए, BRICS MSME Cooperation Portal का इनिश्यटिव लिया गया है। 

हमारे शहरों के बीच best practices साझा करने के लिए BRICS Urban Mobility Hub की स्थापना की गई है। 

Friends, 

भारतीय सभ्यता में प्रकृति को माँ का दर्जा दिया गया है। सदियों से हमारी मान्यता रही है कि विकास और पर्यावरण एक-दूसरे के विकल्प नहीं, पूरक हैं। BRICS में भी हमने मानव विकास और पर्यावरण के बीच संतुलन पर बल दिया है।

यही Sustainability का आधार है। यह भावी पीढ़ियों के प्रति हमारा दायित्व भी है। इस दिशा में हमने कई पहलुओं पर प्रगति की है। 

Smart Grids और Energy Storage के लिए हमने BRICS Digital Centre of Excellence बनाया है। यह हमारे clean energy systems को अधिक reliable, efficient और accessible बनाने में मदद करेगा।

Agro-Ecology और Regenerative Agriculture के Centers of Excellence, पारंपरिक ज्ञान को modern science से जोड़ेंगे। Community-based climate adaptation के लिए तैयार किये गए सिद्धांत, indigenous knowledge को climate action का महत्वपूर्ण आधार बनाएँगे। 

Friends,

इन चारों स्तंभों पर आगे बढ़ते हुए BRICS के माध्यम से हमने inclusive global growth को बढ़ावा देने का प्रयास किया है। क्योंकि हमारा मानना है कि BRICS में विकसित solutions का लाभ केवल ब्रिक्स तक सीमित नहीं रहना चाहिए। इन्हें ग्लोबल साउथ की आवश्यकताओं के अनुरूप adaptable और accessible बनाना चाहिए।

साथियों,

मैं मेरे निजी अनुभव से कह सकता हूं कि BRICS में Global South के देशों का विश्वास बढ़ा है, क्योंकि BRICS में-

उनकी आवाज सुनी जाती है।
उनके अनुभव का सम्मान होता है।
और solutions उनके लिए नहीं, उनके साथ मिलकर बनाए जाते हैं।

BRICS की शक्ति हमारी diversity और cooperation में है। 

We may be rooted in different realities, but together, we rise through cooperation, and blossom for humanity. 

हमारी विविधता हमारी पहचान रहे, हमारा सहयोग हमारी प्रेरणा बने, और हमारी प्रगति पूरी मानवता के काम आए।

आप सबका बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

***********

MJPS/SS/ST

2309663.title: Indian Railways Expands Passenger Connectivity and Freight Capacity in August 2026; Freight Loading Grows by 5.4% Over August 2025
2309663.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Expands Passenger Connectivity and Freight Capacity in August 2026; Freight Loading Grows by 5.4% Over August 2025
14 Services of Amrit Bharat regularised to Strengthen Affordable Rail Connectivity; Services Link Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Other Key Regions in August 2026
5 New Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals Commissioned, Taking Total to 149; Faster Freight Movement to Support Industry and Regional Economic Activity 
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 12:06PM by PIB Delhi

August 2026 witnessed significant expansion in railway connectivity and services across the country, with Indian Railways recording growth in both passenger movement and freight loading. During the month, 14 Amrit Bharat services were regularised, providing more affordable and comfortable travel options to passengers across several important routes, while 5 new Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals (GCTs) were commissioned to improve last-mile freight connectivity for industries.

Indian Railways also recorded 5.4 per cent growth in freight loading, reflecting continued demand from key sectors of the economy. Passenger traffic increased as well, with additional special train services being operated to meet the surge in demand during the festival season.

More Freight Movement, Supporting Industry and the Economy

Indian Railways loaded 137.9 million tonnes of freight during August 2026, compared to 130.9 million tonnes in August 2025, registering a 5.4 per cent year-on-year growth.

The increase in freight movement reflects growing demand from key sectors such as coal, iron ore, steel, fertilizers and other commodities. Higher rail freight movement also helps industries access reliable transportation while supporting the movement of essential commodities across regions.

Freight revenue during August 2026 increased by 6.27 per cent compared to August 2025, indicating continued strengthening of the freight business of Indian Railways.

Higher Movement of Key Commodities Supports Industry and Essential Supply Chains

Several important commodity groups recorded healthy growth during August 2026. Iron Ore loading increased by 12.1 per cent, Clinker by 10.4 per cent, Domestic Container by 9.2 per cent and Coal by 6 per cent. Finished Steel loading increased by 4.9 per cent, Mineral Oil by 3.1 per cent, Fertilizers by 1.6 per cent and Balance Other Goods by 8.2 per cent.

The growth in these segments strengthens the rail-based supply chain for industries and supports the movement of essential inputs and finished goods across the country. Increased container movement, in particular, supports more efficient transportation of diverse goods through the rail network.

5 New Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals to Improve Freight Connectivity

In August 2026, 5 new Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals were commissioned, taking the cumulative number of commissioned GCTs to 149 as on 31 August 2026.

The newly commissioned terminals are at -

  • Shivlakha, Gujarat

  • Nalli, Tamil Nadu

  • Shaktinagar, Uttar Pradesh

  • Deoragram, Madhya Pradesh

  • Brajrajnagar ,  Odisha

The expansion of the Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal network brings freight-handling facilities closer to production and consumption centres. By enabling more direct and efficient handling of goods, these terminals can reduce avoidable movement, improve logistics efficiency and facilitate faster evacuation of freight from industrial and commercial locations.

The growing GCT network is also helping strengthen the integration of railways with India's wider logistics infrastructure, giving industries greater access to rail-based freight transportation.

14 Services of Amrit Bharat were regularised to Expand Affordable Rail Connectivity

August 2026 marked a significant expansion of passenger connectivity, with 14  Amrit Bharat services were regularised from special train to regular train during the month, taking the total number of Amrit Bharat services to 86.

The services connect several major cities and regions, including Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and other important parts of the country.

The services include:

  • Subedarganj - Lokmanya Tilak Terminus

  • Gorakhpur - Bandra Terminus

  • Gorakhpur - Delhi Jn

  • Ahmedabad - Bhagalpur

  • Lokmanya Tilak Terminus - Prayagraj Jn

  • Prayagraj Jn - Udhna Jn

  • Dhanbad - Coimbatore, among others.

These new services are expected to provide passengers with more travel options, improved connectivity between major urban centres & regional destinations and affordable long-distance rail travel.

For Purvanchal and eastern Uttar Pradesh, services from Gorakhpur to Bandra Terminus and Delhi provide additional connectivity to two major metropolitan regions, benefiting passengers travelling for employment, education, business and family purposes.

Similarly, the Ahmedabad-Bhagalpur connectivity strengthens the rail link between Gujarat and Bihar, providing passengers from both regions with another direct travel option. The Dhanbad-Coimbatore service improves long-distance connectivity between eastern India and southern India, particularly benefiting passengers travelling between industrial and employment centres.

Connectivity between Prayagraj and Udhna and between Prayagraj and Mumbai further expands travel options for passengers from Uttar Pradesh travelling towards western India.

The expansion of Amrit Bharat services is part of Indian Railways' continued efforts to provide comfortable, affordable and accessible long-distance rail travel, particularly for passengers travelling between major cities and emerging regional centres.

Passenger Traffic Continues to Grow

Indian Railways carried 67.27 crore passengers during August 2026, compared to 64.43 crore passengers during August 2025.

Suburban passenger traffic recorded particularly strong growth, increasing by 9.02 per cent. A total of 38.01 crore suburban passengers travelled during August 2026, compared to 34.89 crore in August 2025.

The increase reflects the continued importance of the railway network in providing affordable daily mobility to millions of passengers, particularly in densely populated urban and suburban regions.

Additional Special Trains Help Passengers During Festival Rush

With increased passenger demand during the festival season, Indian Railways operated 144 trips of Rakshabandhan Special trains between 25 and 31 August 2026, compared to 48 trips operated between 8 and 14 August 2025.

The substantial increase in special train services helped provide additional travel capacity during the peak festival period, giving passengers more options to travel during a period of exceptionally high demand.

Such additional services are particularly important for passengers travelling to their hometowns and families during festivals, helping ease pressure on regular services and improving travel availability during peak periods.

Expanding Rail Connectivity, Strengthening Everyday Mobility

The developments during August 2026 reflect Indian Railways' continued focus on expanding passenger connectivity, improving travel options, strengthening freight infrastructure and responding to changing demand.

The introduction of new Amrit Bharat services is expanding affordable long-distance connectivity between major cities and regional centres, while additional festival services are helping passengers manage seasonal travel demand. At the same time, the expansion of Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals is strengthening the logistics network and improving rail access for industries.

Through continued capacity augmentation, improved operational efficiency and expansion of passenger and freight infrastructure, Indian Railways remains focused on making rail travel more accessible and strengthening the railway network as an important driver of economic activity and regional connectivity across the country.

*****

Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma

2309656.title: NHRC, India in partnership with Ministry of External Affairs to organise ITEC Executive Capacity Building Programme on human rights for senior-level functionaries of NHRIs of the Global South
2309656.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India in partnership with Ministry of External Affairs to organise ITEC Executive Capacity Building Programme on human rights for senior-level functionaries of NHRIs of the Global South
The 6-day programme will begin on the 14th September, 2026 in New Delhi
The programme aims to provide insights into various dimensions of human rights, international perspectives and share the NHRC, India’s experience to enhance awareness among participants of various NHRIs
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 11:49AM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India in collaboration with the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), is organising a six-day Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) Executive Capacity Building Programme on human rights for senior-level functionaries of National Human Rights Institutions (NHRIs) of the Global South in New Delhi from 14th to 19th September 2026. The programme will be inaugurated by the Chairperson of NHRC, India Justice V. Ramasubramanian.

The programme aims to strengthen the capacities of participating NHRIs and facilitate the exchange of experiences and good practices, with a view to promoting cooperation in the advancement and protection of human rights in their respective countries. The customised programme has been developed based on the needs of participating NHRIs and the feedback received during the four previous ITEC capacity-building programmes organised by the Commission. Forty-one senior-level functionaries from 15 NHRIs are expected to attend.

The programme will cover themes including the development of international human rights framework, contemporary human rights issues, human rights and business, impact of new technology on human rights and sustainable development. Participants will also gain insights into NHRC, India’s functioning, including its complaint management and investigation mechanisms, in the context of global human rights discourse.

Drawing on NHRC, India’s experience of over three decades, the programme seeks to promote mutual learning and meaningful collaboration among NHRIs for advocacy, enforcement and institutional strengthening across the Global South. Eminent persons with domain expertise in capacity building and training will serve as resource persons.

Participants will engage in interactive sessions with leading practitioners, cultural immersion and field visits. The programme will provide opportunities for dialogue and exchange among NHRIs of the Global South, reflecting NHRC, India’s commitment to strengthening human rights institutions and cooperation across the region.

2309659.title: INS KULISH ARRIVES AT REAM NAVAL BASE, CAMBODIA AS PART OF EASTERN FLEET OPERATIONAL DEPLOYMENT
2309659.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INS KULISH ARRIVES AT REAM NAVAL BASE, CAMBODIA AS PART OF EASTERN FLEET OPERATIONAL DEPLOYMENT
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 11:45AM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Indian Navy’s Eastern Fleet Operational Deployment, INS Kulish arrived at Ream Naval Base, Cambodia, on 12 Sep 2026. The visit aims to further strengthen maritime cooperation and enhance professional linkages between the Indian Navy and the Royal Cambodian Navy.

On arrival, the ship was received by representatives of the Royal Cambodian Navy and officials from the Embassy of India in Cambodia.

The programme during the stay will comprise professional interactions, familiarisation visits, sports fixtures and structured naval engagements, providing opportunities for personnel to exchange domain knowledge and enhance operational synergy.

The port call forms part of India’s continuing efforts to expand maritime outreach across the Indo-Pacific and is in keeping with the Act East Policy, the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) and India’s endeavour to promote a free, open and inclusive maritime environment.

2309650.title: 50 Kilometres, Countless Beneficiaries: Mizoram’s Railway Lifeline Completes One Year of Success
2309650.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
50 Kilometres, Countless Beneficiaries: Mizoram’s Railway Lifeline Completes One Year of Success
Within Just One Year, Bairabi-Sairang Railway Line Transforms Travel, Tourism and Logistics in Mizoram, Opening New Horizons for the Hill State
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 11:27AM by PIB Delhi

On 13th September 2025, the inauguration of the 51.38 km Bairabi-Sairang railway line and the Sairang Railway station by Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, opened a new chapter of progress and development for Mizoram. Within just one year, the railway line has brought about transformative development in this remote hill state, and has transformed from just a line on the railway map into a gateway towards improved mobility, greater access to markets, enhanced tourism and new opportunities.

🛤️ Bairabi–Sairang railway line turns One, opening doors to endless opportunities https://t.co/BNXtbuzpOr

— Ashwini Vaishnaw (@AshwiniVaishnaw) September 13, 2026

The Milestone: When the Rails Reached the Hills

For generations, Mizoram’s difficult terrain made long-distance movement heavily dependent on roads, making travel very time consuming, uncomfortable and unrealiable. The commissioning of the Bairabi-Sairang new railway line completed changed the scenario.

(The Bairabi-Sairang line carries the national railway network across Mizoram’s challenging hill terrain)

The Bairabi Sairang railway line is an engineering marvel, traversing the steep hills, deep valleys and gorges of Mizoram. The project comprises 153 bridges, including 55 major bridges, 88 minor bridges and 10 Road Over Bridges/Road Under Bridges. As many as six bridges exceed 70 meters in height, with the tallest rising up to 114 meters, which is 42 metres taller than Delhi’s Qutub Minar. The alignment also passes through 45 tunnels stretching over almost 16 kilometres. The rail corridor connects the national railway network onwards from Bairabi with the four newly developed stations of Hortoki, Kawnpui, Mualkhang and finally the Sairang railway station, thereby completing rail connectivity to the very threshold of Aizawl, the capital of Mizoram.

Thus, the inauguration of the Bairabi Sairang Railway Line on 13th September 2025 fulfilled a long cherished dream of the people of Mizoram, and brought reliable railway passenger and freight services close to the State’s largest centre of population, administration, education and commerce.

 

(Sairang station became Mizoram’s new passenger and logistics gateway to the national railway network)

 

Passenger Mobility: The Numbers tell a story of trust

Three important long distance train services now connect the capital of Mizoram with the cities of Guwahati, Kolkata and Delhi. The Sairang – Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express gave Mizoram its first direct premium railway connection with the national capital, while the Guwahati and Kolkata services created dependable links with major educational, commercial and medical centres across the eastern and northern parts of the country. Further, the Sairang – Silchar passenger train service, which was inaugurated by Hon’ble Union Minister of Railways, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw in January 2026, provided a regular and reliable passenger train service connecting Sairang with the Barak Valley of Assam.

Over the course of the last one year, these train services have completed more than 1100 trips,  becoming an integral part of the lives of the people of Mizoram. The strongest endorsement of the importance of these train services have come from the passengers themselves, receiving the patronage of over 15 Lakh passengers. Passenger demand for these trains have consistently remained very high, with all trains running at over 100% capacity on every trip.

The tri – weekly train service from Sairang to Kolkata has recorded an average occupancy level of over 140 %, while occupany in the daily train service from Sairang to Guwahati has consistently stayed above 110%. The Sairang Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express has similarly achieved an average occupany of over 145 %. These train services have also generated total ticket sales of Rs 54 Crores for the Indian Railways.

During this last one year, Sairang railway station has successfully catered to more than 5.54 lakh passenger movements, with an average of 3300 passengers visiting the station every day. The railway station has not only emerged as a vital hub for passenger travel, but also an integral part of community life in the surrounding area, with local residents carrying out tree plantations and other environmental initiatives around the station complex.

 

 

 

Freight Transformation: Rail Cargo to Aizawl

The Bairabi Sairang Railway line has also brought about transformative change in freight transportation in Mizoram, enabling goods including essential commodities, automobiles and construction materials to reach Aizawl in a safe, time bound and cost effective manner. 

The first railway cargo train arrived at Sairang on 14th September 2025, just one day after the inauguration of the new line, carrying a consignment of more than 26000 bags of cement from STAR Cement Siding at Tetelia near Guwahati. This cargo train had an immediate impact on the prices of cement in Aizawl, clearly demonstrating how railways can drastically reduce logistics costs and contribute to economic development of an entire region. Moreover the direct freight train services bridge the gap in procuring the automobiles, thus reducing the landing cost, making it more pocket friendly to the end consumers. In another notable milestone, the first automobile consignment, consisting of 119 Maruti cars from Changsari near Guwahati, arrived at Sairang by rail in December 2025, transforming automobile logistics in the region. 

In the last one year, more than 2500 wagons of railway freight have been delivered at Sairang. Of these, approximately 70% of the cargo consisted of construction materials like cement, stone and sand, These commodities have supported housing and public works in Mizoram, promoting infrastructure development in the state at lower costs as well as reducing the time required for materials to reach their destinations.

Other railway cargo at Sairang has consisted of essential commodities including rice and fertilizers, as well as 156 wagons containing automobiles.  Automobile rakes have created a safer and higher capacity supply channel for vehicles, while fertilizer and foodgrains have served agriculture and local PDS distribution in the state, shifting bulk movement from long road hauls to efficient railway transport.

(The inaugural cement rake established Sairang as a freight-handling point)

(The 1st Automobile Freight Rake handled at Mizoram)

 

Railway enhances educational and tourism opportunities for people of Mizoram

Direct trains from Delhi, Kolkata, Guwahati and Silchar have made Mizoram easier to reach for domestic travellers. Railway has offered an affordable entry point for visitors who earlier had to depended entirely on air or lengthy road journeys. This has resulted in an overall growth of tourism in Mizoram by over 86% since the introduction of railways. 

The benefits have extended beyond ticketed travel. Greater visitor movement is supporting hotels, homestays, restaurants, taxis, guides, cultural enterprises and local markets. Reliable rail access is also strengthening Mizoram’s ability to host educational, sporting, cultural and official events with wider national participation.

For students of Mizoram, railway connectivity has expanded practical access to universities, professional institutes, coaching centres, examinations and academic events outside Mizoram.

Local Enterprise: From Mizo Hands to National Markets

Railways is also playing an empowering role for popularizing Mizoram’s handloom, bamboo, cane and craft traditions in wider markets. The first parcel consignment from Sairang was booked on 19th September 2025, carrying Anthurium flowers to Delhi through the parcel van of the Sairang Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express. That modest consignment carried a larger message: high-value local produce could begin its national journey from within Mizoram itself.

(The first parcel consignment of Anthurium flowers was booked from Sairang for Delhi)

(Parcel space created a direct channel for delicate and time-sensitive local produce)

 

One Year and Beyond: From Isolation to New Possibilities

In one year, the Bairabi Sairang railway line has demonstrated the far reaching effects of the successful translation of vision into reality. The impact is visible in several directions at once. Passengers have direct access to major cities; students have a more practical route to institutions and examinations; tourists have an affordable gateway; traders receive bulk consignments closer to market; construction and food supplies move with greater capacity; and flowers, crafts and other local products gain a pathway towards national consumers.

The deeper significance of Sairang lies in what it has made possible. A railway line built through difficult hills has compressed distance, widened choice and given Mizoram a new logistics identity. It has linked mobility with dignity, infrastructure with enterprise, and connectivity with opportunity.

(The Sairang-AnandVihar Terminal Rajdhani Express gave Mizoram a direct premium connection with the national capital)

(The Sairang Railway Bridge has a pier of height 114m, which is 42 m taller than Delhi’s Qutub Minar)

2309647.title: Incentive Scheme for Promotion of Domestic PNG Connections
2309647.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Incentive Scheme for Promotion of Domestic PNG Connections
Clean and Affordable Piped Cooking Gas for Every Home
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 11:08AM by PIB Delhi

Overview

Piped Natural Gas (PNG) expansion is an important part of India’s transition towards cleaner household energy and energy security. Supplying PNG to homes is part of City Gas Distribution (CGD) network development. Such a network comprises pipelines and allied facilities that serve households, commercial establishments, and industrial units. Entities authorised by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) develop it. PNGRB has authorised entities in 309 Geographical Areas (GAs). Together, these areas span the entire mainland of the country. As of 18 August 2026, there were 1.74 crore domestic PNG connections across the country.

To expand PNG coverage further, the Incentive Scheme for Promotion of Domestic PNG Connections was launched on 18 August 2026. The Scheme came into effect from 1 September 2026.

About the Scheme

The Incentive Scheme for Promotion of Domestic PNG Connections seeks to accelerate the growth of active domestic PNG connections. It aims to enable households to access clean, safe and affordable cooking gas through piped supply. The Scheme provides incentives to CGD entities for converting unbilled connections into active, billed connections. It also incentivises the expansion of the PNG network into new areas. The Scheme will run in two tranches spread over six months.

A minimum number of connections has been fixed for every Geographical Area under the scheme. During the performance period, eligible CGD entities must add billed domestic connections beyond this threshold. For each such incremental connection, the entity earns an additional allocation of 200 Standard Cubic Metres (SCM) of gas. This gas is domestically produced Administered Price Mechanism (APM) gas, which is priced lower.

The additional allocation will replace the costlier Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG). CGD entities presently buy this LNG for their Compressed Natural Gas (Transport) segment. Substituting it with cheaper APM gas brings down their overall gas sourcing cost.

The payback period on capital spent for a domestic connection is therefore expected to shrink. It is expected to fall from about ten years to nearly three years. Companies therefore gain a strong commercial reason to connect homes faster.

Benefits of PNG for Households

PNG offers several important benefits for households, including ease of use, cost savings, and uninterrupted availability. The following are the key advantages of PNG for household users:

  • Safe and secure: Gas travels through underground pipelines at low pressure, so cylinders need not be stored or handled. Being lighter than air, it rises and disperses quickly in the rare event of leakage.
  • Everyday convenience: No booking, storing or changing of cylinders is required. Gas remains available at home round the clock. Bills are based on metered use, much like electricity or water.
  • Lower costs: A household pays only for the gas it actually uses. On a per-unit energy basis, PNG usually costs less than LPG. Monthly fuel expenses therefore come down over time.
  • Cleaner environment: PNG burns cleaner and gives off fewer pollutants than conventional cooking fuels. Indoor air stays healthier and carbon emissions remain lower.
  • Assured supply: Pipeline supply is continuous and free from the logistics of cylinder delivery. Homes in high-rise buildings and crowded urban colonies benefit the most.

Initiatives for PNG Expansion

PNG expansion is being supported through measures for faster approvals, rationalised taxes, and streamlined infrastructure development. Digital platforms and awareness initiatives are making household transitions to PNG simpler, quicker, and more accessible:

  • Streamlined Regulatory Approvals: An Accelerated Approval Framework has been issued under the Natural Gas and Petroleum Products Distribution (Through Laying, Building, Operation and Expansion of Pipelines and Other Facilities) Order, 2026. The Order also introduces uniform charges for pipeline Right-of-Way (RoW), which cover permission to use land or public areas for laying PNG pipelines. Applications will now be processed on priority and within defined timelines.
  • Reduced Value Added Tax (VAT): States are being encouraged to lower VAT on natural gas to 5 percent. Several States have already done so, making piped gas cheaper for consumers.
  • National PNG Drive 2.0: The nationwide drive was held from 1 January to 30 June 2026 to accelerate DPNG connections across Geographical Areas.
  • Unified PNG registration portal: A single-window digital platform is being developed. It will make applying for and tracking new connections simple and quick.

Towards Cleaner, Connected Homes

Clean cooking fuel at home adds to the comfort, health and dignity of every household. Now in effect, the new Scheme aligns the commercial interests of gas companies with this national goal. As pipelines reach more areas and more kitchens, dependence on cylinders steadily declines. Piped gas is thus set to become a natural part of everyday living in India.

2309642.title: Prime Minister chaired the BRICS session on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism” (September 12, 2026)
2309642.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister chaired the BRICS session on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism” (September 12, 2026)
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 10:48AM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the BRICS session on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism” on September 12, 2026 during the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.

2. In his remarks, Prime Minister emphasized that:

i. Global South is at the front row of global crises, but the back row of decision-making. We must turn the “pyramid of privilege” into a “platform of partnership”.

ii. Global governance must reflect today’s realities, with greater representation especially in institutions such as the UN Security Council.

iii. Efforts must be made to make the Global South move from being a rule-taker to a rule-shaper. Through BRICS, we can provide young diplomats and policymakers from the Global South with negotiation skills, practical training and legal expertise.

iv. Seafarers make a significant contribution to global trade, yet they often lack adequate support during times of crisis and proposed establishing a Seafarers Emergency Support Network.

3. PM concluded by saying that as our future is shared, the right to shape that future must also be shared - from voice to impact, from privilege to partnership. Prime Minister's Opening Remarks may be seen here.

4. The session concluded with the adoption of the New Delhi BRICS Leaders' Declaration, setting the shared priorities, commitment, and direction for BRICS cooperation going forward. The declaration may be seen here.

2309628.title: Dryland Congress 2026 Concludes with Delhi Declaration on Drylands
2309628.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Dryland Congress 2026 Concludes with Delhi Declaration on Drylands
Three-Day Dryland Congress Ends with Call for Science, Innovation and Partnerships to Transform Drylands
Robust Data Systems, Living Laboratories Essential to Build Resilient Dryland Agri-Food Systems: Dr M.L. Jat, Secretary DARE
Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 9:07AM by PIB Delhi

The three-day Dryland Congress 2026 concluded today in New Delhi with a strong call for greater South–South and triangular cooperation to accelerate solutions for dryland agriculture. The final day coincided with the United Nations Day for South–South Cooperation and culminated in the adoption of the Delhi Declaration on Drylands (3D), setting out a shared agenda for transforming dryland agriculture through collaboration, knowledge exchange, innovation and collective action across the Global South. It was endorsed at the closing plenary by participating governments, institutions, partners and delegates of the Dryland Congress 2026.

Addressing the concluding session, Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, emphasised the need to bring foresight to the centre of efforts on dryland agriculture. He called for a strong institutional mechanism and stated that the ICAR-National Institute of Agricultural Economics and Policy Research (ICAR-NIAP) should be mandated to lead foresight work on dryland agriculture. He also stressed the need for robust data and information systems for dryland agri-food systems, as well as common innovation grounds or living laboratories that connect research with practice and policy.

Dr Himanshu Pathak, Director General, ICRISAT, underlined the strategic importance of drylands for global food security and called for the deliberations of the past three days to be translated into concrete action. He emphasised the need to distil the deliberations and prioritise them into short- and long-term actions, moving from ideas to concepts and from concepts to concrete action and implementation by bringing together expertise, knowledge and camaraderie.

The Valedictory Session also highlighted new partnerships and collaborations emerging from the Congress. New agreements and Memoranda of Understanding were announced with the Global Crop Diversity Trust. ICRISAT also exchanged MoUs with Avior Life Sciences, NIFTEM, Wipro Limited, and the Angul and Rayagada District Administrations of Odisha, further strengthening partnerships supporting innovation and action in dryland agriculture. The Co-Chairs of the Congress, Dr D.K. Yadava, DDG (Crop Science), ICAR, and Dr Stanford Blade, DDG (Research & Innovation), ICRISAT, presented a summary of the three-day deliberations and highlighted key outcomes and recommendations emerging from the conference.

Earlier, the day opened with a Commemoration Ceremony for the UN Day for South–South Cooperation, featuring messages from the UN Secretary-General, the FAO Director-General and UNOSSC Director Ms Dima Al-Khatib. Dr Himanshu Pathak, Director General, ICRISAT, shared the vision of the International Solidarity for South-South Cooperation in Agriculture (ISSCA) and highlighted the importance of strengthening partnerships across the Global South. Representatives of ICRISAT, ICAR, CGIAR, RIS, NABARD and the CGIAR Capacity Sharing Accelerator reaffirmed their commitment to advancing South–South cooperation for greater impact.

This was followed by the session “Knowledge Without Borders: Advancing South–South and Triangular Cooperation,” convened with CGIAR. Two panel discussions examined approaches to making South–South and triangular cooperation effective and taking successful models to scale. Speakers from national agricultural research systems in Ethiopia, Senegal, Brazil, China and India, along with representatives from CGIAR, FARA and APAARI shared experiences and perspectives.

The Congress also witnessed the presentation of the ISSCA Global Awards 2026, an annual flagship initiative recognising proven agricultural innovations from institutions across the Global South with strong potential for scale and cross-country adaptation. The inaugural edition received 170 nominations from 34 countries across Asia, Southeast Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Latin America and the Caribbean. The ISSCA Global Award for Transformative Excellence (Mega Award) was presented to ICARDA, Lebanon, for TAAT Wheat Compact Technologies: Heat-Tolerant Wheat Varieties; CIMMYT, Mexico, for e-Agrology 360; and Odisha Livelihoods Mission, Government of Odisha, India, for Women-Led Sustainable Farming for Nutrition and Rural Resilience.

The Crop Improvement & Production Technologies awards went to Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute (BARI), Bangladesh, for BARI Chinabadam-9; University of Agricultural Sciences, Dharwad, India, for GPBD 4; and Department of Agricultural Research (DAR), Myanmar, for climate-smart, early-maturing chickpea, pigeonpea and groundnut varieties. The Natural Resource Management & Climate Resilience awards recognised the Karnataka State Department of Agriculture for Krishi Bhagya; NECTAR, India, for integrated banana pseudo-stem processing; Department of Agriculture, Government of Bihar, for rejuvenating Aahar–Pyne landscapes; and Sustainable Farming Solutions, Malawi, for digital land-restoration stewardship.

The Agribusiness & Market Systems awards recognised BIID Foundation, Bangladesh, for e-Krishok; Tamil Nadu Agricultural University for the TNAU-FPO Linkage Programme; and Nigerian Stored Products Research Institute for its Parabolic-Shaped Solar Dryer. The Digital Agriculture awards went to the Department of Horticulture, Government of Andhra Pradesh, for the APMIP Digital Ecosystem and the Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Co-operation Department, Government of Gujarat, for Krushi Pragati.

The Livestock Improvement & Production Technologies awards recognised WorldFish, Bangladesh, for its improved carp seed system and International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI), Kenya, for the Participatory Indigenous Chicken Breed Improvement Program (PIC-BIP). In addition, 16 Best Poster Awards were presented to students and research scholars, recognising promising research and emerging scientific talent in dryland agriculture.

Held under the theme “Transforming Dryland Agriculture with South–South Cooperation,” the Congress concluded with a renewed commitment to translate scientific knowledge into action, scale proven innovations and strengthen partnerships for resilient and sustainable dryland agriculture across the Global South.

2309578.title: ITRA Jamnagar Organises Three-Day Workshop on Microbiome Research and Health & Wellness
2309578.body_html:
AYUSH
ITRA Jamnagar Organises Three-Day Workshop on Microbiome Research and Health & Wellness
Posted On: 12 SEP 2026 9:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, an Institution of National Importance under the Ministry of Ayush, organised a three-day intensive workshop on “Understanding Health and Wellness through Microbiome Research” from September 9 to 11, 2026.

The workshop aimed to familiarise participants with emerging developments in microbiome research and explore its potential relevance to health, wellness and preventive healthcare from an Ayurvedic perspective.

Prof. Sharmila Mande, Ayush Distinguished Scientist Chair, Ministry of Ayush, and Dr. Tarini Shankar Ghosh, Assistant Professor, IIIT-Delhi, delivered sessions during the workshop and shared insights into contemporary concepts, research methodologies and emerging evidence in microbiome science. The interactions provided participants with an opportunity to understand the potential implications of microbiome research for human health.

The workshop brought together Ayurvedic knowledge and contemporary microbiome science, with discussions covering areas including diet, digestion, metabolism, health promotion and individualised approaches to health and wellness. The programme also highlighted the importance of interdisciplinary and evidence-based research for generating scientifically validated knowledge and strengthening the scientific foundation of Ayurveda.

The workshop concluded with a brainstorming session led by Prof. Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA, to identify potential areas for collaborative and multi-centric research. Discussions explored the scientific investigation of Ayurvedic concepts such as Agni (digestion and metabolism), Ahara (diet), Prakriti, healthy lifestyle practices and Ayurvedic therapies in relation to gut microbial communities.

A total of 52 faculty members and research scholars participated in the three-day workshop. The programme facilitated knowledge exchange, scientific dialogue and identification of future avenues for collaborative research.

The initiative is expected to contribute to strengthening interdisciplinary research at the interface of Ayurveda and modern scientific disciplines. Microbiome research offers potential avenues for studying traditional Ayurvedic concepts through contemporary scientific frameworks and developing evidence-based approaches in areas such as preventive healthcare, nutrition, digestive health, metabolic health and overall wellness.

The workshop is part of ITRA’s continued efforts to promote evidence-based, interdisciplinary and public-health-oriented research in Ayurveda, with the objective of translating traditional knowledge into scientifically validated approaches for promoting health and well-being.

2309538.title: Prime Minister's bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping
2309538.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister's bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping
Posted On: 12 SEP 2026 7:45PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi met with H.E. Mr. Xi Jinping, President of the People’s Republic of China on 12 September 2026, on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi.

The two leaders welcomed the steady progress in India-China bilateral relations since their last meeting in Tianjin in August 2025. They reaffirmed that both countries should take a strategic and long term perspective of their ties. Differences should not become disputes. Prime Minister highlighted that both sides must be guided by three mutuals- mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest.

Prime Minister emphasized that peace and tranquility in the border areas remains an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations. He underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border related issues. The two leaders expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question proceeding from the political perspective of their overall bilateral relations and the long-term interests of the two peoples.

The two leaders took note of the progress in people-to-people ties and underscored the need to further promote cultural exchanges, business linkages and greater mobility between the two countries. On economic and trade relations, they underlined the need to address each other’s concerns, including structural trade imbalance and supply chain issues, and facilitation of meaningful and predictable market access.

The two leaders agreed that both sides must continue to expand common ground on regional and global issues, and in addressing challenges.

Prime Minister appreciated China's support for India's BRICS chairship and its contributions towards the success of the BRICS Summit-2026.

2309536.title: Digital India BHASHINI CEO Addresses Lattice 2026 at IIM Calcutta; Highlights AI Ecosystems for Population-Scale Impact
2309536.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Digital India BHASHINI CEO Addresses Lattice 2026 at IIM Calcutta; Highlights AI Ecosystems for Population-Scale Impact
Annual business conclave held in Kolkata under the theme ‘The Capability Decade’
Posted On: 12 SEP 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi

Lattice 2026, the annual business conclave of the Indian Institute of Management Calcutta (IIM Calcutta), was held in Kolkata today under the theme ‘The Capability Decade’. The conclave brought together students, industry leaders and professionals for discussions on artificial intelligence, technology, innovation, leadership and the capabilities required to create impact in a rapidly evolving technology landscape.

The conclave featured Shri Amitabh Nag, Chief Executive Officer, Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), Digital India Corporation, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), as Chief Guest. He shared insights from India’s experience of building and deploying language technology as Digital Public Infrastructure, with a focus on the challenges of taking AI from models and experimentation to real-world adoption at scale.

Speaking on the challenges of reaching a diverse population, Shri Nag described the digital, language and literacy divides as interconnected challenges and stressed that technology must adapt to people and their contexts. He highlighted the importance of voice-first and multilingual technologies in expanding access, while noting that India’s diversity requires AI systems to account for differences in language, dialect, domain and context.

The practical application of this approach was also demonstrated during the session, with BHASHINI’s Shrutlekh deployed live as Shri Nag spoke, enabling real-time language translation and transcription. The demonstration showcased how language AI can operate in a live setting and support multilingual communication beyond controlled or experimental environments.

The interaction also touched upon the organisational and product choices that shape the success of emerging technologies. Drawing from BHASHINI’s experience, Shri Nag spoke about building with people and for people, including community participation in creating language resources through BhashaDaan. He also underlined the importance of clear use cases, rapid experimentation, learning from failure and short feedback loops in moving from ideas to deployable solutions, while bringing research and product teams closer to real-world requirements.

Reflecting on the experience of building BHASHINI, he said, “The hardest problems we faced were almost never about the model. They were about market design, incentive design, organisational design, and ecosystem design. He further said  “Diversity is new normal “ and we need to adapt fast and quick

The discussion further highlighted the role of partnerships, open infrastructure, co-creation and teamwork in taking technology beyond individual products. He noted that organisations working with emerging technologies need to build a culture of conversation, experimentation, brainstorming and partnership, while creating infrastructure that enables multiple participants to contribute to a larger ecosystem.

The conclave also featured discussions on emerging technologies, business and leadership, with participants engaging on the changing requirements of organisations and professionals in an AI-driven economy. The emphasis on capability building reflected the need to move beyond technological development alone towards building the organisational and ecosystem capacity required for meaningful adoption.

Concluding his interaction with students, Shri Nag encouraged them to look beyond individual applications and consider the larger platforms, standards and ecosystems they can help create. “Ask instead, what ecosystem standard can we establish, and how quickly can we get others to help us build the network effects around it?” he said.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is India's national platform for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI powers over 800 government websites, has enabled more than 9 billion cumulative AI inferences, processes over 24 million AI inferences daily, and supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, making Digital Public Infrastructure more accessible through Language AI.
